Repro, 3 files: schema.av `export type Ref = {…}`, api.av `export use schema.{Ref}`, main.av using Ref. The old path is clean; the layer says resolve.duplicate_type. graph's other refusals (`Kind` `.Bytes` unhandled, the `Decode.fields` misuse) are graph's own, and both paths say them. </to_controller>

payload.result:
Most of those 83 are lint rules (dead_parameter, nullable_flag_local and the like). `check` runs the rules and `build` doesn't, so they're expected and not candidates. Posting half A's ranked list.

<to_controller>
SWEEP, half A: 1,191 of 1,191 done, with suspect rows rerun under the fixed runner. B is pending from wrong-answers. Agree: 1,099. Not fixing anything.
1. SOUNDNESS (old refuses, layer accepts): 32. 30 are expected: 26 use a layer-only form (`tapes --new-only`: ctx, generic methods, type-param defaults, annotations naming fields, state seats); 4 have `differs.why` (the sibling-pin ruling, shown_typed_empty_list).
   Both unexplained ones are the layer RIGHT:
   - graph/repro/generic-ref: `run` answers `p1`; the old derive takes the `.value()` branch for `Ref<T>`.
   - std-db model_stacked: prints its `.expected`; the old path says `language.defect`.
   No soundness hole in A.
2. LAYER FALSE REFUSALS of passing program tests: the real finds. All three are annotations whose compile-time reads of crossing/field facts come back absent or unmatched:
   - features/annotations/tests/doc_and_annotations: annotation.said, "variant crossing did not match".

# The program layer's refusal suite

Each directory here is a package of its own, one case: a source the program layer must refuse
in the old path's words, or must build. `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh` judges them all;
its head says what each file means. In short:

- `refuses.expected`: the old path's `avra check` words, its warnings aside, paths as `<case>`.
  Both the old `check` and `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 avra build` exit 1 saying exactly this.
- `prints.expected`: what the product prints. The old `check` exits 0, the program layer builds
  the package, and its binary prints exactly this.
- `differs.why`: the paths are known to differ here, for the reason on its first line. The case
  is said and not failed while it differs, and fails once it holds until the file goes.
  `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known` lists them.

A new case is a directory with `avra.toml` and `src/main.av`; `PIN=1 sh
tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <case>` gives it the old path's expectation.

WHY HERE AND NOT UNDER A PACKAGE'S `src/`: `avra test` builds every package nested under a
package's sources as a suite of its own (`nested_roots` in compiler/suite.av), so a case that must
be refused would fail that package's tests. Under `tools/` no suite reaches them, as with
`tools/wasm-refuses/`.

Kit revised at 03:25 (/work/sweep-share/one.sh and README). Two runner faults, both mine:
- A library fixture (provider, vendored package, `test_reads`) "declares no entry point", so `build` proves nothing. The runner now runs the layer's `check` on those.
- The cleanup was recursive, so a parent fixture deleted a nested provider's `.avra-cache` mid-build ("object couldn't be written"). It now deletes only the fixture's own cache.

Each keeps its property, read through the layer: `judged`, `provided`, `rule_items`, the layouts,
`code_hash`, `file_docs`, the seat walk and the task survey. Where a layer twin already held a
test's language cases, the old file goes and its remaining cases join the twin.

- bypass_outside_bracket: the live rule's 17 cases read the layer's `findings()` over `provided`
  with the real `@std/meta`. 17/17.
- rule_split: a file's findings equal each declaration's own, judged alone. The licence above
  travels with its declaration; a clean file finds nothing. The layer runs rules item by item. 3/3.
- settle_bill: `judged(src).lowered()`. Layer bodies carry `layouts`, not `reg_types`, so the two
  hand-built registers take a text box and a record box. Added: the run really asks the
  workspace. 3/3.
- slot_names: `CheckedProgram.layout` and `slots()`. Pair and Inner are flat, while Mid and Outer
  are boxed (flatness does not nest). A box spends 1,2,1,1 slots for Outer's fields, 1,2 for Mid's
  and 1,2,1 for Nested's, which is the old a,x,y,mid,s / x,p,q / m,p,q,t. 4/4.
- shape_key: `code_hash(answer)` over the A→B→C→A cycle (and D) keys alike in three declared
  orders, for each type. The guard: B's field the fn reads going string → List<int> moves it. The
  key reads layouts, so a boxed field's insides never move it. 3/3.
- cancel_scc_workspace → cancel_scc_test. Its park cases were already the twin's. Added: a fresh
  task survey asked for `quiet` meets only `quiet`; asked for `pong`, it meets the cycle and
  `leaf`. 5/5.
- writes_scc_workspace → writes_scc_test. Added: on a fresh engine, asking `leaf`'s seat works out
  no cycle seat (`seat_evidence_is_known`); asking `pong`'s works out the whole set and `leaf`.
  6/6.
- error_sites_workspace → error_sites_test. Its raise cases were already the twin's. Added: a
  concretely typed fn raises the error it declares, and two files alike node for node each raise
  only their own error. 8/8. INTERNAL, removed: the ErrorSite rows, `within`, `chain`, the
  `Raised` rows' writer and revisions. They are the old Failures query's tables; the layer infers
  per fn (`raised`).
- seal_order_workspace → seal_order_test, which already holds its property: a write through a
  `mut` seat in another file lands in the record and in its holder. The layer signs nothing in an
  order, so nothing is left to vary.
- structural_workspace → structural_test. Its eleven set cases were already the twin's. Added: a
  view's declaring statement, as the layer reads its item, fingerprints apart on an edit inside a
  sited hole and alike when written the same. INTERNAL, removed: the int place-key edge cases;
  `place_key` and its kin are read only by the old workspace.
- read_set_workspace → read_set_test, which holds every read-set case. INTERNAL, removed: the
  site-lowering cases (hoist, tree, direct, keyed, the plan); `SiteLowering`/`SitePlan` are read
  only by the old compiler/analysis.av. top_level_state_test pins what never-hoisting means at run
  time.
- decl_facts: docs and annotations read through `file_docs` (`///` lines in order, null when none,
  `@name(args)` as written, stacked order, a type's and a const's); `Code.annotations()` through
  `rule_items`. The builtin case becomes: beside a `//!` header, a declaration with no `///` reads
  none, the header being the file's. INTERNAL, removed: the held-row minting cases (old Decls'
  `mint_faced`). `Code.doc()` leaves Code's API: it read the old Analysed tables, and no caller
  remains. 10/10.

Callers: across every package, the only ones were declared()→binding() and is_registry()→answering(), each the other's only caller.
So in the ports commit the four leave Code's API, beside their test cases. declared_ty and answering_arms stay, for bound_value_type and the enums check. The enums check comment that named `Code.answering()` loses the reference.

step F: code, quote_pattern, rule, cell_get_copy and the memory test read the layer's Code

Each reads `Code` the way the program layer hands it to a rule. It uses spec-harness's verbs:
`Judged.rule_items` and rule_examples' `example_roots`. There is no second door to Code.

- cell_get_copy, rule: `fires` and `fix_at` try the rule on the first root of the program's rule
  items.
- quote_pattern: the subject is a Code over the first item's first statement, its answer
  expression or the statement itself. The local `refused_with` is judged's report. 44/44.
- code: `tail` and `find_text` walk the items' roots. The two enclosing_decl cases ask which item
  holds a node: a nested fn's node stands in its outer fn's item, and two siblings stand in two
  items.
  `type()` and the Read-effect purity rows ask inside a body. The rule items type bodies, never
  the entry's own statements, so at the entry `m.get(k)` has no receiver type and reads as
  impure. 7/7.

answering()/is_registry() rows; rule's `declared()` guard pair with its probe `seen_typed`. Those
four projections read the old Analysed tables (`Code.analysed()`), and on the layer's Code they
unwrap absent. No rule the compiler carries calls them; they go with the old path, and nothing on
the layer needs their cover.

/// The program `asked` names made, its objects and binary kept: its shape, then each bucket keyed
/// by the answers it's made of, the program made again only where an object isn't kept.
fn binary_made(engine: QueryEngine, asked: BinaryAsked) -> BuiltBinary {
    let shape = match phased(engine, "the shape", () -> shape_reached(engine, asked.entry)) {
        .At(s) -> s,
        .Unmade(why, at) -> { return BuiltBinary.Unmade(why, at) },
    }
    let hashes = phased(
        engine,
        "the code hashes",
        () -> program_code_hashes(engine, asked.entry).hashes,
    )
    let absent = hashes.find(it.hash == null)
    if absent != null { return BuiltBinary.Unmade(unhashed(), absent!.target) }
    let made = phased(
        engine,
        "the keys",
        () -> keyed_objects(
            engine,
            asked.entry,
            shape,
            hashes,
            objects_salt(engine, asked),
            joined_path(asked.dir, "obj"),
        ),
    )
    bucket_kept(engine, asked, shape, hashes, made)
}

cd /work/avra-l58 && git add packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests/readmit_test.av && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
step F: deletions — twelve tests that pin only the old compiler's internals

Each pins a table, cell or fold the old path keeps and the layer does not have. Each is listed with
the layer test that covers what it was for, or why none needs to.

- build_mode: the old Workspace's compiler_id, object_key_of and build_cache_root. On the layer,
  cli tapes.av `objects_salt` folds compiler, code hash, opt, inlined, target and linked archives
  into every object and link key. No layer test pins that a target moves an object's key (named
  as a gap).
- cutoff_fingerprint: content fingerprints of the Namespace, NameFacts, TypeFacts and Voices folds.
  On the layer every answer is Saved, and a dependent stands when the answer's bytes are equal.
  Covered by decl_grain_test and item_tapes_test (edits that leave answers alike recompute nothing
  past them).
- decl_rows: the Items cell's row hash and reader edges. The layer keys items one by one. Covered by
  item_tapes_test ("one item's body edited … only that item is read") and decl_grain_test.
- direct_test_workspace: pins an idiom rule against a test calling `new_workspace`, which the
  deletion removes. Nothing is left to cover.
- file_module_relation: the old Decls File/Module relation tables. The layer names files by
  SourceFileAddress and keeps no such table. None needed.
- method_rows: the Methods cell's reader edges. The layer dispatches through per-impl queries.
  Covered by decl_grain_test's caller of `b.get()` through `Box`.
- settle_closure: the settlement's closure digest over name buckets. Covered by decl_grain_test ("a
  declaration added keeps every query of main's, answering alike").
- settle_name: the settle interning (settle_id, spelled_settle, settle_symbol). Covered by the same
  decl_grain_test case.
- typed_window: the per-body of_expr and stmt_flags windows. The layer types each item on its own
  tape. None needed.
- warning_facts: the file_facts_wire round trip. The layer keeps findings item-relative. Covered by
  decl_grain_test ("a comment above it keeps every query of main's, answering alike").
- written_where: the receivers pass read inside an open resolve key. Covered by impls_test ("a `let`
  receiver of a writing method is warned", "writing is TRANSITIVE").
- doc_fact: the Decls `@side` DocFact column and `mint_faced`. The layer reads doc and annotations
  off the item (item_docs.av). Covered by cli docs_doc_test ("both come back, doc first", "a fn with
  neither").

readmit_test, an old-path test outside this list, read decl_rows' `items_ordinal`. That helper
moves into readmit_test (22/22 on the old path).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJujuUjfCYmCnDDGZzWu
EOF

- compiler/tests/file_module_relation: INTERNAL — pins the old Decls File/Module relation tables and their pinned handles; the layer names files by SourceFileAddress and keeps no such tables; none needed
- compiler/tests/typed_window: INTERNAL — the old Workspace's per-body of_expr/stmt_flags windows; the layer types each item on its own tape, no file-wide windows; none needed
- compiler/tests/settle_name: INTERNAL — the old Workspace's settle interning (settle_id / spelled_settle / settle_symbol); on the layer a const's settling is a query keyed by its item's keyed id, and decl_grain_test's "a declaration added keeps every query of main's, answering alike" holds that stable across a declaration added above
- compiler/tests/warning_facts: INTERNAL — the old file_facts_wire round trip; the layer keeps findings item-relative and places them only when said, and decl_grain_test's "a comment above it keeps every query of main's, answering alike" covers an edit above leaving them alike
- compiler/tests/written_where: INTERNAL — the old receivers pass read inside an open resolve key (db.begin/settle); the layer answers whether a method writes `self` by its own queries, no resolve to sit inside. Property covered by features/impls/tests/impls_test ("a `let` receiver of a writing method is warned", "writing is TRANSITIVE")
- compiler/tests/settle_closure: INTERNAL — the old settlement's closure digest over name buckets (edges_by_reader, group_print); the layer settles a const by queries per name. That an unrelated declaration added re-settles nothing is covered by decl_grain_test ("a declaration added keeps every query of main's, answering alike")
- compiler/tests/decl_rows: INTERNAL — the old Items cell's row hash and its reader edges (edges_by_reader, value_hash_of); the layer keys a file's items per item. item_tapes_test ("one item's body edited … only that item is read") and decl_grain_test (bodies, comments, blank lines and foreign reads move nothing past their item) cover the property
- compiler/tests/build_mode: INTERNAL — the old Workspace's compiler_id / object_key_of / build_cache_root. On the layer, cli tapes.av `objects_salt` folds compiler, code hash, opt, inlined, target and linked archives into every object and link key, and the store is the tree's (`.avra-cache/tapes`). GAP: no layer test pins that a target moves an object's key; flagged to the lead
- compiler/tests/cutoff_fingerprint: INTERNAL — content fingerprints of the old Namespace/NameFacts/TypeFacts/Voices folds; on the layer every answer is Saved and a dependent stands when an answer's saved bytes are equal. decl_grain_test and item_tapes_test cover edits that leave answers alike recomputing nothing past them
- compiler/tests/method_rows: INTERNAL — the old `Methods` cell's reader edges (edges_by_reader, sig_key); the layer dispatches through per-impl queries. decl_grain_test's caller calls `b.get()` through `Box` and keeps every query across edits in `Box`'s file
- features/impls/generic_traits: PORTED — the old method-table case (registered_methods/declare_method re-run) becomes `judged(realize()+…).clean()`: two members sharing a name at different arguments are two entries, neither declared twice. Re-registering adds nothing is INTERNAL (the layer registers nothing; per-impl queries)
- features/tests/doc_fact: INTERNAL — the old Decls' `@side` DocFact column and `mint_faced`; the layer reads doc and annotations off the item (item_docs.av `file_docs`). cli docs_doc_test covers "a fn with a doc and an annotation: both come back, doc first" and "a fn with neither"
- std-errors errors_adversarial: NOTHING OLD IN IT — it calls no compiler; it runs on the layer, 14/14. Its one tie is the header's prose naming `analyze_source` as the harness it lacks: reworded to `judged` (comment only). Neither INTERNAL nor a port; it stays

or through a callee, answers the state at the call; a pure one answers its constant.

clean, neither declared twice. The layer registers nothing.
annotations, marks: every old read was syntax (fn_parts, annotations_of, enum_parts,

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
root=$(pwd)
out=build/cost
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git fetch -q --depth=1 origin "$snapshot" 2> /dev/null || :
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
    echo "cost: snapshot $snapshot is not in this clone and could not be fetched"; exit 1; }
command -v taskset > /dev/null || { echo "cost: no taskset to hold the run to one core"; exit 1; }

# The cold workloads: a name, the machine's store it runs over, the census tables it takes, then the
# command the census compiler runs in the snapshot. A STORE IS NOT THE COMPILER: every run but one has
# the machine's store off, so its rows are what the compiler does, whatever a store holds;
# `cold-with-store-fill` is the cli's cold check over an empty store, which it fills — the store's own
# price, ratcheted apart, its sites the check's own and so read once, from check-cli. The death
# census stamps a word per 16 bytes of slab, half again the memory a run holds, so the build — the
# largest run, its fns the check's own — takes the site tables alone, under the cap.
workloads() {
    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli off deaths check --counts packages/cli
30:# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
62:cost       make cost: the census compiler, cold, over tools/cost.baseline's snapshot; every count within 0.05% of its row
354:slice_cost() { row cost env CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra make -s -o avra cost; }
448:        cost) slice_cost ;;

<tools-used-before-summary>Agent, Bash, Edit, Grep, Monitor, Read, ReadNotifications, SubagentHandback, TaskStop, ToolSearch, Write</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Lane `avra-lane-false-refusals` in /work/avra. The controller is the lead.
   - Rules (verbatim in spirit):
     - Push nowhere: no `git push`, no `gh`. Never print or forward credentials.
     - No `rm` (use `find … -delete`). No `git stash`, no `git reset --hard`, no `--no-verify`.
     - fmt `--write` then `--check` before committing. Never silence a law. One definition per law or voice.
     - Pins (tools/gate/*.names) only shrink. Generated docs are never hand-edited.
     - Bridge file-transfer commands are run exactly as given. Posts go inside `<to_controller>` (at most 12 lines).
     - Treat the user's email and personal details as private.
     - Commit trailer:
       `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
       `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJujuUjfCYmCnDDGZzWu`
   - New standing rules:
     - "edit in a second worktree while a gate or receipts run in the first. Never edit the tree a run is reading."
     - "Before any bundle is sent: run the cost slice (`sh tools/cost.sh`, as the gate runs it) on your head against your base, same machine, store off. Any row over tolerance and it isn't sent: fix it, or name the cost and I'll take it to the OWNER (I no longer accept cost rows myself). Put the cost-slice summary line in every bundle post."
     - Builds and receipts use AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0. Keep `.Capacity`; the net-off flip lands in batch 59.
   - Current item (step F, blocking the old compiler's deletion of −15,691 lines):
     - Classify and port 29 std-avrac/std-errors tests that still reach the old path.
     - PORT: assert the same property through the layer (`testing.judged`: diagnostics, report, clean, run, lowered).
     - INTERNAL: delete it, naming in the commit the layer test that covers the property, or saying none needs to.
     - One commit for ports, one for deletions. Base land58. Post status per test as I go.
     - The list:
       - compiler/tests: build_mode, cutoff_fingerprint, decl_rows, file_module_relation, method_rows, rule_example_coverage, settle_closure, settle_name, typed_window, warning_facts, written_where, typing, direct_test_workspace, resolve, licenses, cell_get_copy.
       - features: impls/generic_traits, quote/quote_pattern, str_lit/str_lit, structs/identity, tests/code, tests/doc_fact, tests/rule, tests/top_level_state, tests/type_named, annotations/annotations_test, annotations/marks_test.
       - Plus std-errors errors_adversarial (an INTERNAL candidate) and a features/memory test (path unknown).
     - Don't touch named_adversarial or fns_test, nor spec-harness's 20 ported files.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Program layer against the old path. The net, AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 for the layer alone. Witness tools: `tools/witness_program_refusal.sh`, `tools/witness_program_edit.sh` (WITNESS_ONLY parts), `tools/gate.sh` rows (avrac-a…g, edit-a…g, cli, cost).
   - Rounds:
     - Generated ids: `GENERATED_FIRST + round·ROUND_SPAN(2^32) + key`, built by `round_ids_of`.
     - `round_generated(file, r)` is a @cut_query; per-item `made_sites`.
     - Cut queries `made_item` and `made_declared_named(file, name, rounds)`.
     - `GENERATION_ROUNDS = 8`; the depth voice is `annotation.generation_depth`.
   - Ruling (A): quoted items (`file_quoted`, `QUOTED_FIRST`, placeholder `$holeN`), skipping by package, `refused_where_written`.
   - testing.judged / Judged verbs: clean(), report(), made(), lowered(), checked(), diagnostics. Helpers `refused_with`, `refused_in`, `provided`, `answered`.
   - Cost slice: a census compiler over snapshot a6d0d0a0, each count within 0.05% of tools/cost.baseline.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - /work/avra (lane branch), tip e155c5ac on top of 32edfbbe (the land58 merge). Key edits:
     - item_generated.av: rounds; `chain_root` builds `let here = ChainRoot{...}` once; `made_declared_named(engine, file, name, rounds: int)` with no default.
     - item_generators.av: `generator_run`/`handed_values`/`meta_handed` take `rounds`; `handed_values` and `generated` have `rounds: int` required; `written_home(store, a, file)`.
     - item_meta.av: `meta_of_decl(..., rounds: int = 0)`; `span_written_in` uses a comprehension, `sorted_by`, and `type WrittenSpan`.
     - item_context.av: `item_parts`' about part uses `with { id: i.id, quotes: i.text.contains("quote") }`.
     - core/rebuild.av: `moved_by` with `moved()`; `headed_by_hole`.
     - item_generator_problems.av: `pointed_written`, `made_problems_said`, `derive_said`.
     - features/annotations/check.av: `generation_too_deep` (label "the chain begins here") and `derive_said`.
     - tools/gate/cli.names: generated_view's pins removed.
   - /work/avra-l58 (branch avra-lane-false-refusals-stepf from land58). typing_test.av has been rewritten as a port:
     ```
     use @std.avrac.testing.{judged}
     spec "compiler/typing" { ... judged("let x = 1 + 2\nx").diagnostics.is_empty() ... judged("let x = 1 + y").diagnostics.length == 1 ... "let a = 1\nlet = 3\nlet y = 2" length == 1 ... several decls clean ... two erroring bodies in source order (`a` declares / `b` declares) ... judged("x\nlet x = 1").diagnostics.length == 1 }

#!/bin/sh
# THE avra COMMAND — the compiler, hosted by itself. `build/avra` is
# the working binary; it rebuilds from `make avra`, which uses the
# binary that is already there. The seed is the cold path, and it is
# taken only when there is no binary at all.
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# THE CALLER'S DIRECTORY, kept before this script moves to the tree's
# root: a command that reads "the package I stand in" (`explain`)
# roots there, never at the tree — `cd` below rewrites PWD too.
AVRA_CWD="$(pwd)"
export AVRA_CWD
# the link flags a manifest writes as ${LLVM_PREFIX}

Rounds is committed on the lane branch, and full receipts are running there now. This time they include all seven edit-witness rows, so a regression like the last one can't slip through. Nothing will edit /work/avra while they run.

What rounds does:
- **Generated declarations get their own generators.** A declaration a generator made now has the generators it names run over it, in the next round, with each round reading only the rounds before it. That's what fixes `derive_default_silent`: the component `@formed` emits is now composed and refused exactly as the old path says it, at `formed.av:12:47`, "refused by `View`".
- **Warm edits stay local.** Editing one record reruns only that record's chain: two generator runs, one per round.
- **The depth bound.** A chain past 8 rounds is refused once, at the annotation that started it, naming the chain.
- **The old path is unchanged.**

Two things I fixed on the way:
- A generated declaration's places were counted in the wrong file. This affected the declaration itself, its fields, and its marks.
- A derive's problem on the layer read "refused by `@derive`" where the old path names the trait. Hand-written components now read "refused by `View`" too.

If the receipts pass, the bundle and report follow.

cd /work/avra; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
generation in rounds: a generated declaration's generators run over it, in the next round

As ruled: a generated declaration is a declaration. Its annotations run, and its laws judge, as a
written one's do. This fixes derive_default_silent: a component `@formed` emits is now composed, and
its `@attr` mark is refused (`@std/ui:marked-composition`), as the old path says it.

- Rounds. `round_generated(file, r)`: round 0 is what the written declarations' generators make;
  round r is what the generators named by each round r-1 item's declarations make. `file_generated`
  gathers them, up to `GENERATION_ROUNDS` (8).
- Ids carry their round. `GENERATED_FIRST + round·2^32 + key`, the key from the item's meaning and
  nth, as written items' ids are keyed (`round_ids_of`). `generated_rank` is gone: every positional
  use reads ids (`generated_ids`, `is_generated`, `generated_round`), and a generated item's impls
  are read off its own tape.
- Per item, so a warm edit reruns only the rounds its item feeds (condition 1):
  - `made_sites(file, at)` is a query per generated item.
  - `made_item(file, at)` and `made_declared_named(file, name)` are cut queries, so a round's item
    read by id or by name stands while its neighbours move.
  - A round reads only the rounds before it, so there is no cycle.
- Witness, edit-a's new part `rounds`: three records each `@derive(Again)`, each making a record
  `@derive(Count)`. The middle one given a field reruns its chain alone, two generator runs, once a
  round; warm == cold, and back.
- The depth bound (condition 2): a chain past 8 rounds is refused once, at the written annotation
  that began it, naming the chain. The voice is `annotation.generation_depth`: "generation runs
  deeper than 8 rounds: @derive(Forever) → …". Its witness and code row are in place, golden
  rounds_test.av.
- A copied annotation names its generator where its template was written (`written_home`).
- A generated declaration's places are its template's:
  - `meta_place` counts a span of a generated item in the file whose template wrote it;
  - marks' and annotations' spans move with their nodes when a written template is copied
    (`Rebuilder.moved_by`);
  - a problem with a generated declaration points in its template's file (`pointed_written`).
- A generator's problem with a generated declaration is said: the problems law reads generated items
  too (`made_problems_said`).
- A derive's problem is said as refused by its trait (`derive_said`), as the old path says it: a
  written component's `@attr` composition now reads "refused by `View`" on the layer too.

The old path is unchanged (condition 3).

Witnesses:
- rounds_test 2/2: a next-round derive answers 42; the depth bound is refused once.
- derive_component_marked: the layer says the old path's one true refusal, at formed.av:12:47. The
  case is a form only the layer builds, and the old path also adds two refusals of its own, `impl ${0}`
  and `self` in a member default.
- The edit-witness part `rounds`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJujuUjfCYmCnDDGZzWu
EOF

The edit-witness regression has a cause and a fix.

My own commit c4aa476f, already in the batch-58 bundle, made every generator run check whether its template's file is part of the program by reading the package's directory listing. That listing changes whenever any file in the directory is written, so editing one record reran every generator in the file. That check is now cached once per template file. It's recomputed when the listing changes, but its answer stays the same, so nothing rebuilt from it reruns. In the reproduction, editing one of three records now reruns only that record's generator.

# AN INSTANCE'S CHECK READS WHAT ITS RUN CALLS, AND NOTHING IT ONLY HOLDS: a component whose `check`
# calls one fn its instance holds and holds another it never calls, both in a module of their own.
# The fn it never calls edited: the warm build is the cold one, and no instance's check is judged
# again. Taken back, the fn it calls edited: the check is judged again; edited so the check refuses,
# the warm build refuses as the cold one does.
checked_edit() {
    pkg="$tmp/checked"
    mkdir -p "$pkg/src/fns"
    printf '[package]\nname = "checked"\nversion = "0.0.1"\n' >"$pkg/avra.toml"
    fns='export fn fitting(n: int) -> bool { n >= 1 }\nexport fn unsaid(n: int) -> string { "held: ${n}" }\n'
    printf "$fns" >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    printf 'use @std.meta.{Diagnostic, refuse}\nuse fns.{fitting, unsaid}\ncomponent tray {\n    capacity: int = 1\n    fits: fn(int) -> bool = fitting\n    held: fn(int) -> string = unsaid\n    fn check() -> List<Diagnostic> { if (self.fits)(self.capacity) { [] } else { [refuse("a tray this small does not fit")] } }\n}\ntray t { capacity: 3 }\nprintln("${t.capacity}")\n' >"$pkg/src/main.av"
    built() { AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1 "$avra" build "$pkg" >"$tmp/log" 2>&1; }
    made() { built || { echo "witness_program_edit: the checked build failed:" >&2; tail -5 "$tmp/log" >&2; exit 1; }; unsigned_at "$pkg/src/main" "$1"; }
    judged() { grep -oE 'item_instances_checked [0-9.]+s / [0-9.]+s \([0-9]+\)' "$tmp/log" | grep -oE '[0-9]+\)$' | tr -d ')' | awk '{ n += $1 } END { print n + 0 }'; }
    afresh() { find "$pkg/.avra-cache" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || :; find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete; }
    afresh
    made "$tmp/checked.base"
    printf "$fns" | sed 's/held: /kept: /' >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 made "$tmp/checked.warm"
    held=$(judged)
    afresh
    made "$tmp/checked.cold"
    cmp -s "$tmp/checked.warm" "$tmp/checked.cold" || { echo "witness_program_edit: after the held fn's edit the warm product is not the cold one" >&2; exit 1; }
    [ "$held" = 0 ] || { echo "witness_program_edit: a fn the check never calls, edited, judged $held instance checks again" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "witness_program_edit: a fn an instance only holds, edited — warm == cold, no check judged again"
    printf "$fns" >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    made "$tmp/checked.back"
    printf "$fns" | sed 's/n >= 1 }/n >= 0 }/' >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 made "$tmp/checked.warm"
    called=$(judged)
    [ "$called" -gt 0 ] || { echo "witness_program_edit: a fn the check calls, edited, judged no check again" >&2; exit 1; }
    printf "$fns" | sed 's/n >= 1 }/n >= 5 }/' >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    if AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 built; then echo "witness_program_edit: with the fn its check calls edited to refuse, the warm build kept the instance" >&2; exit 1; fi
    grep '^error' "$tmp/log" >"$tmp/checked.warm.said"
    afresh
    if built; then echo "witness_program_edit: with the fn its check calls edited to refuse, the cold build kept the instance" >&2; exit 1; fi
    grep '^error' "$tmp/log" >"$tmp/checked.cold.said"
    grep -q 'a tray this small does not fit' "$tmp/checked.cold.said" || { echo "witness_program_edit: the cold build refused otherwise:" >&2; cat "$tmp/checked.cold.said" >&2; exit 1; }
    cmp -s "$tmp/checked.warm.said" "$tmp/checked.cold.said" || { echo "witness_program_edit: the warm refusal is not the cold one" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "witness_program_edit: a fn an instance's check calls, edited — judged again ($called), and refusing, warm == cold"
}

if [ -z "${WITNESS_ONLY:-}" ] || printf ' %s ' "$WITNESS_ONLY" | grep -q " check "; then
    checked_edit
    [ "${WITNESS_ONLY:-}" = check ] && exit 0
fi

if [ -z "${WITNESS_ONLY:-}" ] || printf ' %s ' "$WITNESS_ONLY" | grep -q " embed "; then
    embedded_edit

packages/std-avrac/src/core/checking.av|        binder: BindSite? = null,|        binder: BindSite? = null,\n        kept: bool = false,
packages/cli/avra.toml|description = "The avra command"|description = "The avra command"\n# a note no law reads
packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }\n    let _ = cache_dir().length
packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av|            "packs ${before.length} → ${after.length} · bytes ${octets_of(before)} → ${octets_of(after)} · ${distinct([p.print for p in after]).length} compiler(s) kept"|            "packs ${before.length} → ${after.length} · ${distinct([p.print for p in after]).length} compiler(s) kept"
packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(0, (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }|fn cycle_a(n: int) -> int { if n > 0 { cycle_b(n - 1) } else { 0 } }\n\nfn cycle_b(n: int) -> int { if n > 0 { cycle_a(n - 1) } else { 0 } }\n\nfn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(cycle_a(2), (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }'

The merged tree (64f6be87) builds with the net off, and its receipts against base57 are partway through. So far: fmt has no differences, idioms are clean, both program-runs packages pass, and gate a passes. When they finish I'll send `base57..HEAD`.

Rounds are written in i5 but not yet built or tested, because a build now would compete with the gates for memory:
- **Generated ids carry their round:** a generated item's id is `GENERATED_FIRST + round × 2^32 + a key`. The key comes from the item's meaning, as warm's scheme does for written items, so an edit that leaves an item's meaning alone leaves its id alone.
- **Each round reads only the rounds before it.** `round_generated(file, r)` makes round r from per-item `made_sites` queries over round r−1's items. That avoids the cycle that blocked this before. `file_generated` gathers the rounds, up to 8.
- **Depth bound:** beyond 8 rounds it says "generation runs deeper than 8 rounds" and names the chain of generators (`annotation.generation_depth`), with a witness and code row.
- **Problems on generated declarations are now said.** A generator's problem with a generated declaration used to be dropped silently, which is exactly why `derive_default_silent` printed nothing.
- **Witnesses:**
  - A new spec, `rounds_test`, covers a next-round derive answering `42` and the depth refusal.
  - The ask's case `derive_component_marked` expects the `marked-composition` refusal at the template. It has a `differs.why`, because the old path adds two false refusals of its own.
  - A `rounds` edit-witness, added to gate row edit-a, shows that editing one record reruns only its own chain: two generator runs, one per round.

#!/bin/sh
# A WARM EDIT BUILDS WHAT A COLD BUILD OF THE EDIT BUILDS, on the program layer.
# A no-op build over a cold store first builds the cold product. Then for each
# edit: the store the cold build left, the edit, a warm build with every fold
# held to its body (AVRA_FOLD_CHECK) — then the same edited tree built cold; the
# two unsigned products must be one file (a layered product compares as
# `unsigned_at` below says). Then the edit taken back, built warm
# over the edited tree's cold store, must be the first cold product. The edits:
# a literal, a literal in a file of queries, two that change how many task tests
# a body holds (the change a placement keyed by test position trapped on), one in
# the cli and one in another package, an enum given a variant and a record given
# a field, and a method given a seat: one with a default its caller in another
# file leaves out, one that caller is changed to fill, and one with a default
# the impls of a gathered trait in other files leave out; then a defaulted seat
# added and renamed twice, each built over the store the one before left; a line added to the
# cli's manifest, which re-judges that manifest alone; a call added to a body the program already
# reaches, a body's only call of another dropped, so that one leaves the program, and two bodies
# calling each other called anew, so taken back, the pair is cut loose of everything reaching it
# and must leave the program though each still calls the other. Empties every
# `.avra-cache` under packages/ and its own machine store.
# Then AN INFERRED ERROR FOLLOWS ITS REACH: in a package of its own, a fn a `?` reaches gains a
# `fail` of a new type; the warm build must be the cold one, and taken back, the first cold product.
# Then A LAW FOLLOWS ITS ITEM: in a package of its own, an impl's method renamed to a name an earlier
# impl took; the warm refusal must be the cold one word for word, and taken back, the first cold product.
# First, A FILE A BUILD READS AS DATA IS AN INPUT: a package whose consts read one
# file through `provided` and another through `embed`; the first file edited, the
# warm build must be the cold one, worked out again through that file's read and
# the const that reads it alone; taken back, the first cold product.
#   sh tools/witness_program_edit.sh [compiler]   (default build/avra-try, built
#   through the program layer and standing beside build/avra)
#   WITNESS_ONLY="7 8" runs just the edits of those numbers, counted from one;
#   WITNESS_ONLY=embed runs the embedded file's edit alone; WITNESS_ONLY=rename the seat renamed
#   twice; WITNESS_ONLY=infer the inferred error's alone; WITNESS_ONLY=check the instance check's edits;
#   WITNESS_ONLY=derived one of three derived records' alone; WITNESS_ONLY=gathered a member appended to
#   a collect gathered in closure, which a const folds.
#   WITNESS_ONLY=lawed a law's edit alone; WITNESS_ONLY=modes the cli built in each mode over a store
#   the other left, working ahead and alone (modes-whole, modes-layered: one mode's).
set -eu
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$root"
76:edit-a     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY="embed infer composed gathered check lawed derived"
77:edit-b     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=1
78:edit-c     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=5
79:edit-d     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=10
80:edit-e     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=rename
81:edit-f     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-whole
82:edit-g     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-layered
420:# the edit witness's edits `$1`
421:edit_part() { row edit-witness env WITNESS_ONLY="$1" sh tools/witness_program_edit.sh build/avra; }

content.content:
# A member default reading a prop silences a derive-emitted component's refusals

base56 (a73903d2) compiler, gen-2. `avra check .` prints nothing and exits 0. Drop the `tally`
component from src/main.av, or make its default a literal (`state n: int = 0`), and the check
says `error[@std/ui:marked-composition]: … and `title` is marked `@attr`` as it should (the cli
test commands/tests/generated_view_test.av holds that). A hand-written bad composition is still
refused, so only components a derive emits lose their refusals.

It reaches every package that imports std-ui once `field` seeds `state value` from
`self.initial` (std-ui item 2), so generated_view_test goes red there.

@derive(Gen)

# A derive module's private type shadows the landing file's own type

**The law:** generated code reads the provider's private names only where the template itself
names them, and never shadows a name the landing file declares.

- `provider/` is a package whose derive module, `src/gen.av`, declares a private
  `type Held = { reaches: string }`. Its template never spells `Held`. It holds the
  annotated type through `${t}` holes only: once in type position (the answer) and once as
  a record literal's head.
- `user/` depends on `provider`, declares its own `type Held = { n: int }`, and wears
  `@derive(Gen)`.
- `control/` is the same pair, except that the provider's private type is named `Kept`.

payload.result:
The six `decl_grain_test` reds are still there; it's a different cause than I first fixed.

That test edits `lib`, then checks the caller recomputes no more queries than a bystander that doesn't reach `lib`. The caller's build asks `file_quoted(lib)` (whether lib's templates refuse), but the bystander only asks for lib's warnings, which never ask it. So the caller recomputes one query name the bystander doesn't. `lib` writes no template at all, so asking was wasted work anyway.

The fix: only a file whose text contains `quote` is asked for its quoted items. Every other file asks nothing beyond its items, which both sides already ask. i4 is rebuilding to rerun `decl_grain_test` and the template spec.

Idioms are clean now, and `template_judged_test` (4/4) and `quote_test` (16/16) held on the last build. If both pass, I'll commit and rerun the full receipts.

input.command:
cd /work/avra-i4; git add -A packages tools; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
program layer: a template is judged where it is written, once, in the package that wrote it

Ruling (A). A refusal inside a template is its author's. It is said in the check of the package
that writes the quote, at the quote, once. It is never said again in each program that splices it.

- Quoted items (file_quoted, ids from QUOTED_FIRST). Each declaring quote of a file's written items
  is opened where it is written. It is copied through the splice door with every hole filled by a
  placeholder of its own (`$holeN`), which no program can write. It becomes an item no file
  declares and nothing runs, judged by every law. Its fns are typed through its own item. Its
  impls are typed even where a hole names the target, with a receiver of no type it can know.
- What a fill decides stays the instance's:
  - a finding on a hole, or one holding a hole (a name's resolution only on one);
  - one where the quote opens, where a fill with no place of its own lands;
  - one reading a placeholder;
  - whether a fn may read `self` (where it lands decides if it is a method);
  - a name a hole that lands seats or statements may bind.
  A template's reads of the names it declares stand. A binder a hole names never reads by its
  written name, so that read is still the template's.
- Downstream (the ruling's cut, at the package line). A generated item holding none of the checked
  package's writing is not judged here: it is the template's package's to judge. In any generated
  item, a finding at a node another package's template wrote is dropped. A lowering refusal in such
  an item is its template's, said where the template is written (refused_where_written), not a
  defect. file_erring counts what the file's diagnostics say, so the two never disagree.

Witnesses:
- features/quote/tests/template_judged_test.av (4/4, red before): the provider's own check refuses
  a template's body, a method over a hole's type, and nothing of a template whose holes are all
  that vary; a dependent hears the template's refusal once, at the template.
- generated_fn_body_judged, generated_method_body_judged (its provider now holds only its one
  template) and refuses_in_wrapped_body hold. The dependent build says the provider's refusal.
- generated_hole_bound_read: differs.why. Opened where it is written, the read of `x` is undefined
  in the provider's own file. The old path says resolve.hole_bound at each program that fills it.
- quote_test: the shared fixture's `holed` generator moved to a provider of its own, since its
  template is now refused where it is written. Its test says the provider's words. 16/16.
- False refusals found and fixed on the way: std-meta `match self` in a template fn; std-program
  saved_derive (one placeholder merged two names); std-relation `value` and `k` (seats a run hole
  lands). check of std-avrac, std-program, cli, std-meta, std-relation: no new finding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJujuUjfCYmCnDDGZzWu
EOF

payload.result:
The base57 merge is resolved and committed as c2c08857, but it doesn't build, so I haven't bundled `base57..HEAD`. I've posted this to the lead as a blocker.

`@derive(Saved)` on `Seating` runs out of its 5 MiB compile-time budget. base57 alone fits. My branch adds one variant, `.Capacity`, which says that a `produce` or `channel` capacity isn't an `int`. That came from my earlier lane, which didn't ride batch 57, and that one variant tips the derive over. I confirmed it with three different builders, the last being base57's own freshly built compiler: base57 builds, the merge doesn't, and std-program and std-meta are identical between them.

Separately, base57's committed bootstrap seed refuses base57's own std-text, so building from that seed fails even on base57 itself.

I gave the lead three options:
- **Raise std-avrac's budget** in its manifest under `[lifted]`, re-measured. The design allows this, but it's a manifest decision.
- **Lighten the `Saved` derive** for large enums. That code is std-program's, shared, not mine.
- **Drop `.Capacity`.** I don't recommend it: no existing variant fits, so the refusal would name the wrong thing.

Meanwhile, ruling (A) continues in i4, which builds from 3e377552 without base57. It's rebuilt with the latest rule (a name a hole lands is the instance's). A sweep is running with each compiler checking its own tree:
- the five template witnesses;
- the layer's `check` of std-avrac, std-program, cli, std-meta and std-relation, compared i3 against i4;
- the quote and annotations feature suites.

# THE ONLY RULE THAT LINKS BY HAND, and the one a cold tree and every
# recovery must take — `seed` and `avra` link through the compiler.
# So the object list is named ONCE: a prerequisite and a link line
# spelling it twice were two definitions nothing kept in step, and the
# gap opens silently the instant the variable grows.
#
# AND RECOVERY STOPS HERE. `make bootstrap` continues into `make avra`,
# which overwrites this clean compiler with one built from the CURRENT
# source — so a source that traps while compiling itself (a probe in an
# analysis path, a broken pass) has no way back: every rebuild traps
# again. `make recover` is that way back.
recover: $(COMPILER_OBJS) build/seed.ll
	@mkdir -p build
	@clang -w -O1 -rdynamic build/seed.ll $(SEED_LINK_OBJS) \
	    $(LLVM_LINK) -o build/avra

- **Keyed item ids, a point for the lead:** my branch carries avra-lane-warm b3113115, the keyed item ids, which neither base56 nor base57 holds. One base57 loop in `item_rules.av` counted items by position, which would read the wrong items under keyed ids, so it now walks every item id instead.
- **Not in base57:** laws-fusion's held mechanism isn't there, so there's no second definition to reconcile.

Ruling (A) in i4 is still uncommitted. I've added one more rule from the std-relation templates. A name read by its written name stays the instance's when the template has a hole that lands whole parameters, statements or a block's last statement, because those names read by their written names where the code lands. A binder named through a hole (`let ${x}`) is still the provider's error, since hygiene keeps it apart. After the receipts I'll merge c2c08857 into i4. The real-code baseline gets redone with each compiler on its own tree, since my last sweep mixed them.

content.thinking: Gen-2 means running `make avra` twice, and since the i4 sweep is still using the shared memory pool, I'm checking its progress before starting the builds.

content.content:
$(LLVM_LINK) -o build/avra
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra 2>/dev/null || true
	@echo "recover: build/avra from the seed — a clean compiler, not rebuilt from source"

# Bootstrap hands out GEN-2. A change to lowering or memory reaches a
# compiler's own body only when a compiler already carrying it compiles
# that body, so the seed's gen-1 rebuilds once more.
#
# UNLESS THE SEED IS THIS TREE. `make seed` records the source hash it
# emitted from, and when that hash is the tree's own the seed already IS
# the compiler this source emits — linking it (`recover`) is the whole
# build, and a self-compile only rebuilds the same compiler byte for
# byte. A hash that differs means the seed's codegen MAY lag the source,
# and the two builds stand.
bootstrap: recover
	@h=$$(sh tools/sources_hash.sh); s=$$(cat bootstrap/seed.sources 2>/dev/null || echo none); \
	if [ "$$(sh tools/seed_is_tree.sh "$$h" "$$s")" = seed ]; then \
	    echo "bootstrap: the seed IS this tree — no self-compile"; \
	else \
	    echo "bootstrap: gen-1, the source compiled by the seed"; \
	    $(MAKE) -s avra || exit 1; \
	    echo "bootstrap: gen-2, the source compiled by gen-1"; \
	    $(MAKE) -s avra || exit 1; \
	    echo "bootstrap: build/avra is gen-2"; \
	fi
	@$(MAKE) -s ready

# THE TREE A PROGRAM BUILDS IN: every package's C object, which a native
# link names, and the wasm runtime with the wasm package objects, which a
# page's build names. Without a wasm toolchain here the second half is
# skipped, spoken — a page build then refuses by name.

# THE EDIT LOOP: the source built by the STANDING compiler into
# build/avra-try, never over it — so the builder's print, and every row its
# store holds, stands from one edit to the next. `./avra-try` runs it. A
# change the compiler must READ to build itself (codegen, the front end, a
# refusal about its own source) reaches the product only through `make avra`.
try: $(COMPILER_OBJS)
	@sh tools/capped.sh build/avra-try-build.out 200000 env AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release ./avra build packages/cli --time || { cat build/avra-try-build.out; exit 1; }
	@grep '^time: ast' build/avra-try-build.out | grep -oE 'held [0-9]+/[0-9]+' || true
	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra-try.next && mv -f build/avra-try.next build/avra-try
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra-try 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@echo "try: build/avra-try — ./avra-try runs it"

# THE WARM EDIT LOOP, measured: a one-edit check and build of the cli, and `make try` on a leaf and a core edit.
edit-loop:
	@sh tools/db_measure/edit_loop.sh

	@h=$$(sh tools/sources_hash.sh); s=$$(cat bootstrap/seed.sources 2>/dev/null || echo none); \
	if [ "$$(sh tools/seed_is_tree.sh "$$h" "$$s")" = seed ]; then \
	    echo "bootstrap: the seed IS this tree — no self-compile"; \
	else \
	    echo "bootstrap: gen-1, the source compiled by the seed"; \
	    $(MAKE) -s avra || exit 1; \
	    echo "bootstrap: gen-2, the source compiled by gen-1"; \
	    $(MAKE) -s avra || exit 1; \
	    echo "bootstrap: build/avra is gen-2"; \
	fi
	@$(MAKE) -s ready

# THE TREE A PROGRAM BUILDS IN: every package's C object, which a native
# link names, and the wasm runtime with the wasm package objects, which a
# page's build names. Without a wasm toolchain here the second half is
# skipped, spoken — a page build then refuses by name.

# THE EDIT LOOP: the source built by the STANDING compiler into
# build/avra-try, never over it — so the builder's print, and every row its
# store holds, stands from one edit to the next. `./avra-try` runs it. A
# change the compiler must READ to build itself (codegen, the front end, a
# refusal about its own source) reaches the product only through `make avra`.
try: $(COMPILER_OBJS)
	@sh tools/capped.sh build/avra-try-build.out 200000 env AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release ./avra build packages/cli --time || { cat build/avra-try-build.out; exit 1; }
	@grep '^time: ast' build/avra-try-build.out | grep -oE 'held [0-9]+/[0-9]+' || true
	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra-try.next && mv -f build/avra-try.next build/avra-try
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra-try 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@echo "try: build/avra-try — ./avra-try runs it"

# THE WARM EDIT LOOP, measured: a one-edit check and build of the cli, and `make try` on a leaf and a core edit.
edit-loop:
	@sh tools/db_measure/edit_loop.sh

out=[]; pos=0; odd=0; done=0
for m in pat.finditer(s):
    o,t=m.group(1),m.group(2)
    def split(x):
        x=x.rstrip('\n')
        mm=re.match(r'^(\s*)(.*?)( -> .*)$', x, re.S)
        if not mm or '\n' in x: return None
        return mm.group(1), [v.strip() for v in mm.group(2).split(' or ')], mm.group(3)
    so,st=split(o),split(t)
    if so and st and so[2]==st[2] and all(var.fullmatch(v) for v in so[1]+st[1]):
        names=lambda l:[v.split('(')[0] for v in l]
        merged=st[1]+[v for v in so[1] if v.split('(')[0] not in names(st[1])]
        rep=st[0]+' or '.join(merged)+st[2]+'\n'
        extra=[v for v in so[1] if v.split('(')[0] not in names(st[1])]
        print('hunk',done+odd,'merged; ours-only:',extra)

    out.append(s[pos:m.start()]+rep); pos=m.end()

print('merged',done,'left',odd)

pat = re.compile(r'<<<<<<< [^\n]*\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n', re.S)
ms = list(pat.finditer(s))
m = ms[idx]
ours, theirs = m.group(1), m.group(2)

payload.result:
Ruling (A) is close in i4, but nothing is committed yet; this is where it stands.

**Working now:**
- A provider's own `check` refuses an error inside its template, once, in its own file. That covers the fn body, the method in `impl ${t}`, and an unknown helper.
- A dependent's `build` says the provider's error once, at the provider's file, instead of repeating it at each instance. The defect voice no longer fires.
- `template_judged_test` is 4/4 and `quote_test` 15/16 on the last run. Its 16th case, the template calling an unknown helper, has a fix built but not yet rerun.
- Of the five witnesses, four hold: `generated_fn_body_judged`, `generated_method_body_judged` (its provider trimmed to its one template, expectation re-pinned), `refuses_in_wrapped_body`, and `template_unparsed_said_once`.

**One witness is a deliberate known difference:** `generated_hole_bound_read`. In its own file, a template that reads `x` by its written name after `let ${x} = 1` can't know a hole will name `x`, so the provider now says "`x` is not defined", once. The old path said `resolve.hole_bound` at each program that fills it. The `differs.why` records this, and you can overrule the wording.

**False refusals found in real templates, all fixed:**
- std-meta: `self` read inside a template fn. Whether that fn is a method is decided where it lands, so it's left to the instance.
- std-program: "`end` is not defined". I caused this myself by filling every hole with one placeholder name, which merged fns a hole names; each hole now gets its own.
- Placeholder reads that landed at the quote's opening.

**A test fixture changed as a result:** the suite's shared quote provider held a template that is now refused in its own file (the `holed` generator). I moved it into its own provider for the one test about it.

**Running now:** the five witnesses, both feature suites, and the layer's `check` of std-avrac, std-program, cli and std-meta, against i3 to catch any new false refusals in real code. The cost measurement against the +2% budget, full receipts, then commit and bundle follow.

Ruling (A) is working in i4 for three of the four new cases, but none of it is committed yet:
- **Provider's own check:** a template's body error is refused in the provider's file, at the template, once.
- **Dependent:** a program splicing the template hears the error once, at the provider's file, instead of again at each use.
- **Holes:** a template whose holes stand for a type, a name and a value says nothing of its own.

The run also turned up a real false refusal in std-meta's own templates. A fn written in a template was refused for reading `self` ("not a method"), though it only becomes a method once a hole places it inside an impl. Whether a template's fn may read `self` is now left to where it lands.

The fourth case, a method on an impl whose target is a hole (`impl ${t}`), is fixed but not yet confirmed. Its methods are now typed with a receiver of unknown type.

i4 is rebuilding in the background. It will then run the spec, `quote_test`, and the five witnesses: the three earlier template cases (which should now be said from the provider's quote), `refuses_in_wrapped_body`, and the unparsed-template case. After that come findings across std-avrac, std-program and cli to catch new false refusals in real code, then the cost measurement against laws-fusion's +2% budget.

#!/bin/sh
# THE PROGRAM LAYER REFUSES WHAT THE OLD PATH REFUSES, IN ITS WORDS, AND BUILDS WHAT IT BUILDS.
# Each case under tools/program-refusals/ is a package of its own:
#   refuses.expected — the source must be refused: the old path's `check` and the program
#     layer's `build` each exit 1, and what each says, its warnings aside, is exactly this text;
#   prints.expected — the source must not be refused: the old path's `check` exits 0, the
#     program layer builds it, and what the product prints is exactly this text;
#   target — a case for another target, its triple: each path BUILDS it for that target, the build's
#     refusal is its words, and a printing case's module runs under node (`tools/run_wasm.mjs`); on a
#     machine with no toolchain for the target, both paths refuse in the toolchain's same words, exit 2,
#     and the case is said untooled, neither held nor failed;
#   warns.expected — beside either: each path's warnings, their first lines in the order said, are
#     exactly this text (for a case only the program layer builds, that layer's warnings); an
#     empty one says no warning is said;
#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
known=0
untooled=0
alone=0
for name in $names; do
    why="$cases_dir/$name/differs.why"
    judged "$name" 2>"$tmp/$name.why"
    judgement=$?
    if [ "$judgement" = 3 ]; then
        held=$((held + 1))
        alone=$((alone + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 2 ]; then
        echo "$name: untooled — no toolchain here for $(cat "$cases_dir/$name/target"); both paths refuse alike"
        untooled=$((untooled + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 0 ]; then
        if [ -e "$why" ]; then
            echo "$name: holds now, yet differs.why says the paths differ — take the file away"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        else
            held=$((held + 1))
        fi
    elif [ -e "$why" ]; then
        echo "$name: known to differ — $(head -1 "$why")"
        known=$((known + 1))
    else
        cat "$tmp/$name.why"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
    fi

# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
known=0
untooled=0
alone=0
for name in $names; do
    why="$cases_dir/$name/differs.why"
    judged "$name" 2>"$tmp/$name.why"
    judgement=$?
    if [ "$judgement" = 3 ]; then
        held=$((held + 1))
        alone=$((alone + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 2 ]; then
        echo "$name: untooled — no toolchain here for $(cat "$cases_dir/$name/target"); both paths refuse alike"
        untooled=$((untooled + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 0 ]; then
        if [ -e "$why" ]; then
            echo "$name: holds now, yet differs.why says the paths differ — take the file away"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        else
            held=$((held + 1))
        fi
    elif [ -e "$why" ]; then
        echo "$name: known to differ — $(head -1 "$why")"
        known=$((known + 1))
    else
        cat "$tmp/$name.why"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
    fi

program layer: a template whose file didn't parse is not copied; a body reaching lowering unjudged is a defect

A copy of a template whose file did not parse is neither judged nor lowered: the generator copies
nothing from it, so `build` says only that file's parse refusal, as `check` does
(template_unparsed_said_once). Lowering's catch-all now speaks as a `language.defect`: a body that
reaches lowering has been judged, so the next path that skips judging is loud.

A finding in a generated item belongs to whoever wrote the node it stands on, found by the narrowest
node holding it: a template's file, or the program's own (a body an annotation moves aside, a
field's rule a hole carries in), whose spans count from the program's file. A program-written
finding the site's written item already says is said once (refuses_in_wrapped_body). A generated
item over a declaration a law refuses is not judged: the refusal speaks for it (a duplicated
`grammar` no longer cascades into its door). Format grammars record their site like other
generators. rules_test's three rule refusals now hold on the layer.

Here's where i3 stands (uncommitted). The lead's main witness holds, but not everything is green yet.

**Holding now:**
- **Unparsed template:** `template_unparsed_said_once` says the same single parse refusal under the old path's `check`, the layer's `build` and the layer's `check`. The defect voice is in place. It isn't pinned yet.

The design is at the end of my last message; I'll start building it once these two reds are fixed. The cost measurement comes after (A), since (A) is what changes the cost.

  - The body's statements and arms hold **placeholders**.
  - `store.mark_quote_at(e)` indexes the quote by its item-relative `span.lo`. `quote_at(offset)` is at core/store.av:996-1005.
- **Holes have no node variant of their own.** A hole is an ordinary node whose name is `${k}`, which no program can write (core/holes.av:1-4).
  - `hole_name(text) -> HoleName{parts, holes}` and `placeholder(...)` are at holes.av:21-47.
  - The seat decides the kind (`HoleKind`, holes.av:65-90): Expression (`Expr.Ident("${k}")`), Name (any Scoped/Plain/Nominal text), Binder (`Pat.Bind`), Type (`TypeRef.name`), Statement or Tail (an `ExprStmt` of a lone ident, see `store.hole_stmt` / `bare_hole`, store.av:1224-1233), Arm, Run, Fields, Inits.
  - A run hole `..${xs}` is marked on the fill expression (`is_run_hole`, store.av:665-682). A param spread uses `SeatSpread.Hole(index)` (nodes.av:858-878). `TypeRef.spliced` is at nodes.av:668-686.
- **Classifying holes:** `hole_kinds` and `quote_kind` (Expr/Stmts/Arms/Decls/Holes) are at core/rebuild.av:218-248.

## 2. How a splice fills holes (compiler/sugars.av)
- **Filler:** a filler is `fn(HoleKind) -> Filled` (core/rebuild.av:20-32), called at the hole's seat by `Rebuilder.filled` (rebuild.av:729).

  - A fill of the wrong shape goes to `misfits`. `Unplaceable` goes to `unplaceable`.
- **`template_copied`** (sugars.av:168-198) is private. It does five things:
  - takes the written `Scratch`, or else a re-parse of the woven parts;
  - builds `copier(src, dst, fills, hole_runs, door)`;
  - calls `seated_copy` (229-262), which gives Fields its params, Inits its literal's fields, and every other seat `rb.stmts`/`rb.arms`;

- **New nodes:** `minted_expr` / `minted_stmt` (rebuild.av:633-677) allocate new nodes in `dst` and keep the source spans. A fill with no span is placed at its hole (`placed_fill`, 736).
- **`Splice`** (409-579) turns `@std.meta.Node` values into fills. `generated_spliced` (367-388) adds `lambdas_apart` and `binders_apart`.

//! `quote { … }` — a TEMPLATE: generated code as a value, parsed
//! where it is written. The body is ordinary Avra — statements,
//! declarations, or match arms — and `${e}` is a hole typed by the
//! seat it stands in (`core/holes.av`). The value names this quote
//! and carries its fills: `@std.meta.Code`, `Stmts`, `Arms` or
//! `Decls`, by what the body parsed as. The template's own names
//! resolve here; a name arriving through a hole resolves where the
//! code is spliced.
use features.{LanguageFeature}
use @std.grammar.{Grammar, Rule, Alt, Seq, Item, Prim, Rep, Build, Expect, Recover}
use diagnostics.{DiagCode}

export fn quote_lit() -> LanguageFeature {
    let codes = table<DiagCode> {
        kind                   | summary
        "type.quote_hole"      | "a hole takes what its seat takes"
        "type.quote_meta"      | "a `quote` answers a `@std.meta` value, which this program does not load"
        "type.quote_pat_shape" | "a `quote` pattern matches one node — one statement, no arms"
        "type.quote_pat_subj"  | "a `quote` pattern reads code — a `Code`, not this subject's type"
        "type.quote_pat_hole"  | "a `quote` pattern's hole names a fresh variable, not a written expression"
        "type.quote_pat_type"  | "a `quote` pattern takes no hole in type position yet"
        "type.quote_pat_seat"  | "a `quote` pattern's hole cannot bind at this seat — an embedded name/binder hole, or an arm hole"
        "type.quote_pat_mixed" | "a `quote` pattern's binder is used at both a code seat and a name seat"
        "type.quote_pat_run"   | "two run holes with nothing between them — no scan can split them"
    }
    LanguageFeature quote_lit {
        name: "quote"
        gram: grammar {
            primary = q:quote_lit -> q
            quote_lit = "quote" open:"{" ( arms:arm | stmts:stmt | BREAK )* close:"}" ( begins:HOLE_BEGIN ( holes:hole_content )? ends:HOLE_END )* -> Expr.Body by quote_written
            pattern = body:quote_lit -> Pat.Quote
            nonbind_pattern = body:quote_lit -> Pat.Quote
            hole_content = run:".." name:NAME -> Expr.Ident | e:expression -> e
        }
        diags: codes
    }
    quote_lit
}
