1	//! WHAT A FILE'S ANNOTATIONS MAKE: the declarations a generator writes beside a declaration that
2	//! names it, a trait's under `@derive` or a declaring annotation's, each an item of its file after
3	//! the written ones, read back and signed as one. Each copied node carries the file whose template
4	//! wrote it, so a type it names is read there. A wrap's item holds the wrapper under the fn's own
5	//! name and the written fn moved to its body's name.
6	//!
7	//! What a generator makes over a declaration is a saved answer keyed by the declaration's tape and
8	//! the generator's made program, so it runs once per change of either. A generator the program
9	//! layer doesn't make says why instead.
10	use core.{
11	    template_file,
12	    template_home,
13	    INFERRED,
14	    Expr,
15	    ForeignOrigin,
16	    Scoped,
17	    Stmt,
18	    StmtId,
19	    SyntaxArena,
20	    flatten,
21	    new_node_store,
22	    seat_spelled,
23	    some_list,
24	    spelled,
25	}
26	use @std.meta.{Diagnostic, Directive, Node, derive}
27	use @std.program.address.{SourceFileAddress}
28	use @std.program.answer_record.{ContentHash}
29	use @std.program.query_engine.{QueryDefinition, QueryEngine}
30	use @std.program.saved_derive.{Saved}
31	use @std.program.saved_query.{cut_query, definitions_of, ListedQuery, query, query_definition}
32	use @std.program.source_facts.{PlacedTape, item_tape}
33	use @std.program.syntax_tape.{SyntaxTape}
34	
35	/// Declarations one generator made over one declaration, on one tape, and whether they wrap it: hold
36	/// the fn it's written as, under its own name, and its written body moved aside. A method's wrap
37	/// holds its moved body as a method of its owner, and its wrapper apart, on a tape no file declares:
38	/// the body the written method is read as. `site` is the written item whose declaration the
39	/// generator stood on, by id, once a site has made it.
40	@derive(Saved)
41	export type GeneratedItem = { tape: SyntaxTape, wraps: bool = false, wrapper: SyntaxTape? = null, site: int? = null }
42	
43	/// What generators made, in the order their declarations are written, and what they said instead
44	/// wherever they made nothing or the splice couldn't place what they made.
45	@derive(Saved)
46	export type GeneratedItems = { items: List<GeneratedItem>, said: List<string>, problems: List<KeptProblem> = [] }
47	
48	/// What a generator said about the declaration it ran over, kept whole: its words, where it points —
49	/// a span in the file `home` spells by package and path, absent for the declaration itself — its own
50	/// kind, and whether it only warns; then the site it ran at — the item, the declaration — and what
51	/// ran there: `@std/meta`'s `delegate` over a `collect enum`, else the annotation's name.
52	@derive(Saved)
53	export type KeptProblem = {
54	    message: string,
55	    help: string?,
56	    kind: string?,
57	    warning: bool,
58	    at: FindingAt?,
59	    home: string?,
60	    item: int = -1,
61	    owner: string = "",
62	    by: string = "",
63	    from: string = "",
64	    trapped: bool = false,
65	    unplaced: bool = false,
66	    /// A template naming a file this program does not read, the file's name its message.
67	    unread_home: bool = false,
68	    /// A template whose file did not parse, the file's name its message: nothing is copied from it,
69	    /// and nothing is said of it here, since that file's parse is what is said.
70	    unparsed_home: bool = false,
71	    /// A validator the program layer didn't run, for what it doesn't cross yet: counted, never said.
72	    unrun: bool = false,
73	}
74	
75	/// What a site hands its generator past the declaration it stands on: each argument, and what the
76	/// item writing each declaration among them means, so a site runs again when one changes.
77	@derive(Saved)
78	export type Handing = { args: List<HandedArg>, meanings: List<ContentHash> }
79	
80	/// What `generator` makes over the declaration `file` writes as `name`, its item's tape meaning
81	/// `_declaration`, the generator's made program printing as `print`, handed `handed`; a method of the
82	/// impl `method` where it's one.
83	@query
84	export fn generated(
85	    engine: QueryEngine,
86	    file: SourceFileAddress,
87	    _declaration: ContentHash,
88	    name: string,
89	    generator: GeneratorAt,
90	    print: ContentHash,
91	    handed: Handing,
92	    method: MethodSite?,
93	) -> GeneratedItems {
94	    let l? = generator_program(engine, generator, print) else { return said_only(generator_moved(generator)) }
95	    match generator_run(
96	        engine,
97	        l,
98	        generator,
99	        file,
100	        name,
101	        handed.args,
102	        lifted_budgets(engine, file.package_name),
103	        generator_plan(print, l),
104	        method,
105	    ) {
106	        .Ran(made, problems) -> {
107	            let made_here = items_spliced(engine, file, name, made, method)
108	            made_here with { problems: made_here.problems.concat([kept_problem(p) for p in problems]) }
109	        },
110	        .Stopped(why, fault, said) -> if said { said_only([why]) } else { stopped_run(engine, generator, why, fault) },
111	        .Trapped(why) -> unsettled_run(why),
112	    }
113	}
114	
115	/// A run of `g` that its site stopped before it began, for `why`: said where `g` judges and the
116	/// program is at `fault`, counted where `g` judges and the layer can't hand it what it takes.
117	fn stopped_run(engine: QueryEngine, g: GeneratorAt, why: string, fault: bool) -> GeneratedItems {
118	    if !judges(engine, g) { return said_only([why]) }
119	    if fault { unsettled_run(didnt_run(g, why)) } else { unrun(didnt_run(g, why)) }
120	}
121	
122	/// `g` named as a run that didn't happen, and why.
123	fn didnt_run(g: GeneratorAt, why: string) -> string { "`${annotation_named(g)}` didn't run: ${why}" }
124	
125	/// A validator's run the program layer couldn't make, for what it doesn't cross yet: kept as a
126	/// problem no law says, which the layer's gaps count.
127	fn unrun(why: string) -> GeneratedItems {
128	    said_only([why]) with { problems: [
129	        KeptProblem {
130	            message: why,
131	            help: null,
132	            kind: null,
133	            warning: false,
134	            at: null,
135	            home: null,
136	            unrun: true,
137	        },
138	    ] }
139	}
140	
141	/// A run that didn't settle, kept as the problem its site says: `why`, as an annotation that could
142	/// not run.
143	fn unsettled_run(why: string) -> GeneratedItems {
144	    said_only([why]) with { problems: [
145	        KeptProblem {
146	            message: why,
147	            help: null,
148	            kind: null,
149	            warning: false,
150	            at: null,
151	            home: null,
152	            trapped: true,
153	        },
154	    ] }
155	}
156	
157	/// What the generators every declaration of a file names make, in the order written, then what each
158	/// format gives the record it reads.
159	@cut_query
160	export fn file_generated(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> GeneratedItems {
161	    gathered_items(
162	        [site_generated(engine, file, site) for site in generator_sites(engine, file)]
163	            .concat(format_generated(engine, file)),
164	    )
165	}
166	
167	/// What the validating annotations every declaration of a file wears say of it: no item, only their
168	/// problems. Apart from what the file's generators make, so nothing a validator's own body needs of
169	/// its package — an impl a generator there makes — waits on the validator's run.
170	@cut_query
171	export fn file_validated(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> GeneratedItems {
172	    gathered_items([site_generated(engine, file, site) for site in validator_sites(engine, file)])
173	}
174	
175	/// Each validator the program the package `package` roots reads didn't run, for what the program
176	/// layer doesn't cross yet: a gap of the layer's, never a pass.
177	export fn package_unrun(engine: QueryEngine, package: string) -> List<KeptProblem> { [p for f in program_files(engine, package) for p in file_validated(engine, f).problems if p.unrun] }
178	
179	/// Every problem a generator or a validating annotation kept about a declaration of `file`.
180	export fn file_problems(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> List<KeptProblem> { file_generated(engine, file).problems.concat(file_validated(engine, file).problems) }
181	
182	/// What the generators the fn `file` writes as `name` wears make: what the written declaration
183	/// names, never what generated items do.
184	export fn fn_generated(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, name: string) -> GeneratedItems {
185	    let d? = file_declares_named(engine, file, name)
186	        .names
187	        .find(it.name == name && it.kind == ItemKind.Fn) else { return said_only([]) }
188	    gathered_items(
189	        [site_generated(engine, file, site) for site in declaration_sites(engine, file, d) if !validates(engine, site.generator)],
190	    )
191	}
192	
193	/// What the generators the method `name` of the impl `m` wears make.
194	export fn method_generated(engine: QueryEngine, m: MethodSite, name: string) -> GeneratedItems {
195	    gathered_items([site_generated(engine, m.at.file, x) for x in method_sites_of(engine, m, name)])
196	}
197	
198	/// Several sites' items and words, in order.
199	fn gathered_items(made: List<GeneratedItems>) -> GeneratedItems {
200	    GeneratedItems {
201	        items: flatten([m.items for m in made]),
202	        said: flatten([m.said for m in made]),
203	        problems: flatten([m.problems for m in made]),
204	    }
205	}
206	
207	/// The quote the file `home` names holds at the offset `at` of its text, as the written item holding
208	/// it reads back: the store holding it and the quote; absent where none does.
209	fn written_quote(engine: QueryEngine, home: string, at: int) -> Scratch? {
210	    let file? = template_file(home) else { return null }
211	    let i? = quote_item(engine, file, at).first() else { return null }
212	    let store = read_item(engine, file, i).store
213	    let q? = store.quote_at(at - item_start(engine, file, i)) else { return null }
214	    Scratch { store: store, body: q, start: item_start(engine, file, i) }
215	}
216	
217	/// The written item of `file` holding the quote at the offset `at` of its text, none where none
218	/// does: the item whose text holds the offset, where a quote stands there in it.
219	@query
220	fn quote_item(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<int> {
221	    [i for i in item_ids(engine, file) for start in [item_start(engine, file, i)] if start <= at &&
222	        at < start + item_under(engine, file, i).text.length &&
223	        read_item(engine, file, i).store.quote_at(at - start) != null]
224	        .take(1)
225	}
226	
227	/// Every item of `file` by id: its written items, then its generated ones, each in order.
228	export fn every_item_id(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> List<int> {
229	    item_ids(engine, file)
230	        .concat([generated_id(k) for k in 0..file_generated(engine, file).items.length])
231	}
232	
233	/// Whether `file` holds the item `at`, written or made by its generators: an item a law over bodies
234	/// reads, since a generated body is code and gets every law a written one gets.
235	export fn item_stands(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> bool {
236	    item_held(engine, file, at) || generated_at(engine, file, at) != null
237	}
238	
239	/// The items of `file` that stand before the item `at`, by id, in order: for a written item, the
240	/// written ones before it; for a generated one, every written item and the generated ones made
241	/// before it; every written item where the file holds no `at`.
242	export fn items_before(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> List<int> {
243	    let ids = item_ids(engine, file)
244	    let k? = generated_rank(at) else {
245	        let rank = ids.index_of(at)
246	        return if rank < 0 { ids } else { ids.take(rank) }
247	    }
248	    ids.concat([generated_id(j) for j in 0..k])
249	}
250	
251	/// Where the item `at` stands among every item of `file`, counted from the first: a written item by
252	/// its place among the written ones, a generated one past them all by its place among those made;
253	/// past every written item for one the file doesn't hold. Read without what generators make.
254	export fn item_order(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> int {
255	    let ids = item_ids(engine, file)
256	    let k? = generated_rank(at) else {
257	        let rank = ids.index_of(at)
258	        return if rank < 0 { ids.length } else { rank }
259	    }
260	    ids.length + k
261	}
262	
263	/// What a file's generated items declare, each by its generated id.
264	export fn generated_declares(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> Declarations {
265	    Declarations {
266	        names: [tape_declared(file, generated_id(k), n) for k, g in file_generated(engine, file).items for n in g.tape.declares],
267	    }
268	}

270	/// What one site's generator makes, or why its generator isn't made.
271	export fn site_generated(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, site: GeneratorSite) -> GeneratedItems {
272	    let made = generator_print(engine, site.generator)
273	    let print? = made.print else { return said_only([made.unmade]) }
274	    let handed = Handing {
275	        args: site.handed,
276	        meanings: [item_meaning(engine, d.file, d.item) for h in site.handed for d in handed_decl(h)],
277	    }
278	    let made_here = generated(
279	        engine,
280	        file,
281	        item_meaning(engine, file, site.item),
282	        site.name,
283	        site.generator,
284	        print,
285	        handed,
286	        site.method,
287	    )
288	    made_here with { items: [g with { site: site.item } for g in made_here.items], problems: [p with { item: site.item, owner: site.name, by: annotation_named(site.generator), from: site.generator.file.package_name } for p in made_here.problems] }
289	}
290	
291	/// The declaration an argument hands, where it hands one.
292	fn handed_decl(h: HandedArg) -> List<HandedDecl> { match h { .Decl(d) -> [d], rest -> [] } }
293	
294	/// What the item `at` of `file` means: its tape's meaning hash, a generated item's own.
295	fn item_meaning(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int) -> ContentHash {
296	    let made = generated_at(engine, file, at)
297	    if made != null { return made!.tape.meaning_hash }
298	    let item = item_under(engine, file, at)
299	    item_tape(engine, item.text, item.context).meaning_hash
300	}
301	
302	/// The declarations directives' sources make over what `file` writes as `name`, spliced as one
303	/// item; a wrap's beside the written fn moved to its body's name, its wrapper signed as the written
304	/// fn is, and a twin beside it; a method's wrap with its moved body a method of its owner and its
305	/// wrapper apart.
306	fn items_spliced(
307	    engine: QueryEngine,
308	    file: SourceFileAddress,
309	    name: string,
310	    made: List<Directive>,
311	    method: MethodSite? = null,
312	) -> GeneratedItems {
313	    let unread = flatten([unread_homes(engine, d.source!.node) for d in made if d.source != null])
314	    if !unread.is_empty() { return homes_unread(unread) }
315	    let unparsed = flatten(
316	        [unparsed_homes(engine, d.source!.node) for d in made if d.source != null],
317	    )
318	    if !unparsed.is_empty() { return homes_unparsed(unparsed) }
319	    let spliced = generated_spliced(
320	        [d.source!.node for d in made if d.source != null],
321	        template_home(file),
322	        (home: string, at: int) -> written_quote(engine, home, at),
323	    )
324	    let wraps = made.any(it.wraps)
325	    if wraps && method != null { return method_wrap(engine, method!, name, spliced) }
326	    let moved: StmtId? = if wraps { moved_body(engine, file, name, spliced.store) } else { null }
327	    let unwrapped = if wraps { wrap_said(spliced.store, spliced.stmts, name, moved) } else { [] }
328	    let twins = [twin_of(engine, file, name, d.twin, spliced.store) for d in made if d.source == null && !d.twin.is_empty()]
329	    let stmts = spliced
330	        .stmts
331	        .concat(some_list(moved))
332	        .concat(flatten([some_list(t) for t in twins]))
333	    GeneratedItems {
334	        items: if stmts.is_empty() || !unwrapped.is_empty() { [] } else { [GeneratedItem { tape: tape_of_item(spliced.store, stmts), wraps: wraps }] },
335	        said: spliced
336	            .refused
337	            .concat(if twins.any(it == null) { [twin_unmade(name)] } else { [] })
338	            .concat(unwrapped)
339	            .concat(
340	                if stmts.is_empty() && made.all(it.twin.is_empty()) { some_list(unplaced(made)) } else { [] },
341	            ),
342	        problems: [KeptProblem {
343	            message: w,
344	            help: null,
345	            kind: null,
346	            warning: false,
347	            at: null,
348	            home: null,
349	            unplaced: true,
350	        } for w in spliced.unplaced],
351	    }
352	}

354	/// Each file a template among `n` and the nodes it holds names that this program does not read.
355	fn unread_homes(engine: QueryEngine, n: Node) -> List<string> {
356	    match n {
357	        .Template(home, _, _, fills) -> if home_read(engine, home) { [] } else { [home] }
358	            .concat(flatten([unread_homes(engine, f) for f in fills])),
359	        .Interp(_, holes) -> flatten([unread_homes(engine, h) for h in holes]),
360	        .Many(items) -> flatten([unread_homes(engine, i) for i in items]),
361	        .Name(_) or .Text(_) or .Int(_) or .Float(_) or .Bool(_) -> [],
362	    }
363	}

365	/// Whether the file `home` names is one this program reads: a source of the package it names.
366	fn home_read(engine: QueryEngine, home: string) -> bool {
367	    let at? = template_file(home) else { return false }
368	    package_sources(engine, at.package_name, "src").contains(at.path_in_package)
369	}
370	
371	/// Each file a template among `n` and the nodes it holds names whose text did not parse.
372	fn unparsed_homes(engine: QueryEngine, n: Node) -> List<string> {
373	    match n {
374	        .Template(home, _, _, fills) -> if home_unparsed(engine, home) { [home] } else { [] }
375	            .concat(flatten([unparsed_homes(engine, f) for f in fills])),
376	        .Interp(_, holes) -> flatten([unparsed_homes(engine, h) for h in holes]),
377	        .Many(items) -> flatten([unparsed_homes(engine, i) for i in items]),
378	        .Name(_) or .Text(_) or .Int(_) or .Float(_) or .Bool(_) -> [],
379	    }
380	}

429	/// A method's wrap over the method `name` the impl `m` writes: its written body moved to its body's
430	/// name as a method of the impl's owner, beside what else the directives declare, and the wrapper
431	/// they make of its name apart.
432	fn method_wrap(engine: QueryEngine, m: MethodSite, name: string, spliced: SplicedDecls) -> GeneratedItems {
433	    let store = spliced.store
434	    let moved = moved_method(engine, m, name, store)
435	    let unwrapped = wrap_said(store, spliced.stmts, name, moved?.moved)
436	    let wrapper = spliced.stmts.find((s) -> store.fn_parts(s)?.name == name)
437	    if !unwrapped.is_empty() || moved == null || wrapper == null { return said_only(spliced.refused.concat(unwrapped)) }
438	    let beside = [s for s in spliced.stmts if s != wrapper!]
439	    GeneratedItems {
440	        items: [
441	            GeneratedItem {
442	                tape: tape_of_item(store, beside.concat([moved!.held])),
443	                wraps: true,
444	                wrapper: tape_of_item(store, [wrapper!]),
445	            },
446	        ],
447	        said: spliced.refused,
448	    }
449	}

454	/// The method `name` the impl `m` writes, read into `store` under the name a wrap moves its body to,
455	/// marked as it's written, in an impl of its own for the type the written one is for.
456	fn moved_method(engine: QueryEngine, m: MethodSite, name: string, store: SyntaxArena) -> MovedMethod? {
457	    let stmts = read_into(
458	        engine,
459	        m.at.file,
460	        store,
461	        m.at.item,
462	        item_start(engine, m.at.file, m.at.item),
463	    )
464	    let read = ReadItem { store: store, stmts: stmts, written: store.expr_count() }
465	    let held? = impl_stmt_at(read, m.at) else { return null }
466	    let s? = store.impl_parts(held)!
467	        .fns
468	        .find((x) -> store.fn_parts(x)?.name == name && store.is_static(x) == m.statics) else { return null }
469	    let parts = store.fn_parts(s)!
470	    let moved = store
471	        .alloc_stmt(
472	            Stmt
473	                .FnDecl(Scoped(moved_name(name)), parts.tparams, parts.params, parts.ret, parts.body),
474	            store.stmt_span(s),
475	        )
476	    let marks = store.marks_at(s)
477	    store.update_marks(moved, (_m) -> marks)
478	    let alone? = match store.stmt(held) {
479	        .ImplDecl(of, of_args, target, target_args, _) -> Stmt.ImplDecl(of, of_args, target, target_args, [moved]),
480	        rest -> null,
481	    } else { return null }
482	    MovedMethod { moved: moved, held: store.alloc_stmt(alone, store.stmt_span(held)) }
483	}

485	/// What a wrap of `name` among `stmts` says instead of standing: that it makes no fn of the name
486	/// beside the written one `moved`, or one whose signature isn't the written fn's; nothing for one
487	/// that stands.
488	fn wrap_said(store: SyntaxArena, stmts: List<StmtId>, name: string, moved: StmtId?) -> List<string> {
489	    let wrapper = stmts.find((s) -> store.fn_parts(s)?.name == name)
490	    if moved == null || wrapper == null { return [wrap_unmade(name)] }
491	    if signature_spelled(store, wrapper!) != signature_spelled(store, moved!) { return [wrap_unsigned(name)] }
492	    []
493	}

495	/// A fn's signature as written: its type parameters, each seat's promises and type, and its answer.
496	fn signature_spelled(store: SyntaxArena, s: StmtId) -> string {
497	    let parts = store.fn_parts(s)!
498	    let seats = [seat_spelled(
499	        p.promises.mutable,
500	        p.promises.settled,
501	        if p.ty == null { INFERRED } else { spelled(p.ty!) },
502	    ) for p in parts.params]
503	    "<${[t.name.of for t in parts.tparams].join(", ")}>(${seats.join(", ")}) -> ${spelled(parts.ret)}"
504	}

523	/// The twin a directive asks for beside the fn `file` writes as `name`, read into `store`: a fn
524	/// named `twin`, signed as the written one, answering what a call of it with its own seats answers;
525	/// absent when the file writes no fn of the name.
526	fn twin_of(
527	    engine: QueryEngine,
528	    file: SourceFileAddress,
529	    name: string,
530	    twin: string,
531	    store: SyntaxArena,
532	) -> StmtId? {
533	    let d? = file_declares_named(engine, file, name)
534	        .names
535	        .find(it.name == name && it.kind == ItemKind.Fn) else { return null }
536	    let s? = read_into(engine, file, store, d.item, item_start(engine, file, d.item))
537	        .find((x) -> store.fn_parts(x)?.name == name) else { return null }
538	    let parts = store.fn_parts(s)!
539	    let at = store.stmt_span(s)
540	    let call = store
541	        .alloc_expr(
542	            Expr
543	                .Call(Scoped(name), [], [store.alloc_expr(Expr.Ident(p.name), at) for p in parts.params]),
544	            at,
545	        )
546	    store.alloc_stmt(Stmt.FnDecl(Scoped(twin), parts.tparams, parts.params, parts.ret, call), at)
547	}

587	/// How two generated items differ, where their nodes stand and the files that wrote them aside: the
588	/// first statement and method that mean something else; absent when alike.
589	export fn item_difference(one: SyntaxTape, other: SyntaxTape) -> string? {
590	    let ours = unhomed(one)
591	    let theirs = unhomed(other)
592	    if ours.tape.meaning_hash.same_as(theirs.tape.meaning_hash) { return null }
593	    if ours.stmts.length != theirs.stmts.length { return "${ours.stmts.length} statements, the other's ${theirs.stmts.length}" }
594	    for j, s in ours.stmts {
595	        let t = theirs.stmts[j]
596	        if ours.store.stmt_fingerprint(s) == theirs.store.stmt_fingerprint(t) { continue }
597	        return "statement ${j}${method_differing(ours.store, s, theirs.store, t)} means something else"
598	    }
599	    "its meaning, though every statement's fingerprint agrees"
600	}

1	//! The walk that REBUILDS a template's body. At the quote's build it
2	//! CLASSIFIES every hole by the seat it stands in; at the splice it
3	//! COPIES the body into the target store with the holes filled. One
4	//! exhaustive registry, two roles — a node nobody rebuilds cannot be
5	//! spliced, and the build says so.
6	//!
7	//! The registry is DERIVED (`@derive(Rebuild)` on `Expr`, `Stmt` and
8	//! `Pat`): a payload's TYPE says what happens to it, so the arms are
9	//! a reading of the node model rather than a second copy of it. Two
10	//! variants are SEMANTIC and keep their hand-written method — a
11	//! nested quote's body is copied verbatim, a sublanguage's expansion
12	//! replaces its holes.
13	
14	use @std.relation.engine.{list_cell}
15	
16	/// What a hole is filled with — one shape per `HoleKind`, and ONE
17	/// for a fill that no seat can hold. `Unplaceable` carries the words
18	/// rather than a flag: the splice cannot re-derive why, and a fill
19	/// the compiler cannot place is SPOKEN and never spliced quietly.
20	export enum Filled {
21	    Expr(e: ExprId)
22	    Exprs(es: List<ExprId>)
23	    Name(text: string)
24	    Names(texts: List<string>)
25	    Type(t: TypeRef)
26	    Stmts(ss: List<StmtId>)
27	    Arms(arms: List<Arm>)
28	    Params(ps: List<Param>)
29	    Inits(inits: Inits)
30	    Pat(p: PatId)
31	    Unplaceable(why: string)
32	}
33	
34	/// A literal whose run was refused: no fields, and nothing more to say.
35	export fn spoiled_inits() -> Inits { Inits { names: [], values: [], spoiled: true } }
36	
37	/// A record literal's fields: each name beside its value, in order —
38	/// `spoiled` when a run among them was refused, so the literal says no
39	/// more.
40	export type Inits = { names: List<Plain>, values: List<ExprId>, spoiled: bool = false }
41	
42	/// A hole no seat can hold: which hole, and the words for it.
43	export type Unplaced = { hole: int, why: string }
44	
45	export type Rebuilder = {
46	    src: SyntaxArena,
47	    dst: SyntaxArena,
48	    // the fills by hole index, each materialized AT ITS SEAT and by
49	    // the seat's kind — so a fill's nodes mint just before the node
50	    // that holds them, as a parsed child does; empty while classifying
51	    fills: List<fn(HoleKind) -> Filled>,
52	    // whether the walk MINTS: a classifying walk allocates nothing
53	    copying: bool,
54	    // a nested quote's body is copied VERBATIM: its placeholders are
55	    // its own, not this template's
56	    verbatim: bool,
57	    // classified: each hole's kind by its index
58	    kinds: List<HoleKind>,
59	    // whether each hole was written `${..name}` — a RUN, by its
60	    // index; the mark rides the hole's own FILL expression
61	    // (`q.holes[k]`), never the placeholder standing in its seat, so
62	    // it is read once here and carried by index from then on
63	    runs: List<bool>,
64	    // minted: the nodes that wear the TEMPLATE's origin — every node
65	    // but one whose binder or read came through a hole
66	    made_exprs: List<ExprId>,
67	    // the source node each made expression was copied from, aligned
68	    // with `made_exprs` — a copied node may itself have been minted
69	    // by a sublanguage of another file
70	    made_from: List<ExprId>,
71	    made_stmts: List<StmtId>,
72	    made_pats: List<PatId>,
73	    // HOLED nodes: their own binder or read resolves where the code
74	    // lands (never wearing the template's origin, `made_exprs`'s own
75	    // rule), but their SPAN is still the template's own offset — a
76	    // node minted here is never rewritten to point at the splice
77	    // site. `note_spanned` marks these separately from `made_exprs`
78	    // so an error about one is homed at the template without also
79	    // resolving its name there.
80	    holed_exprs: List<ExprId>,
81	    holed_stmts: List<StmtId>,
82	    holed_pats: List<PatId>,
83	    // a seat or lambda param whose NAME came through a hole: a binder
84	    // with no node of its own, keyed by its ParamId
85	    holed_params: List<ParamId>,
86	    // each binder a lone hole's fill built, whose name binds where the code lands
87	    filled_pats: List<PatId>,
88	    // every seat the copy made, each keeping the template's span
89	    made_params: List<ParamId>,
90	    // each statement whose name seats a hole filled, with those seats
91	    landed: List<LandedAt>,
92	    // the holes whose fill did not fit their seat — a defect the
93	    // splice speaks, never a program that compiles wrong
94	    misfits: List<int>,
95	    // the holes whose fill no seat can hold, each with the words the
96	    // splice speaks — a LAW the writer broke, not a defect
97	    unplaceable: List<Unplaced>,
98	    // the open nodes, innermost last: whether a name of each came
99	    // through a hole
100	    holed: List<bool>,
101	    // how a copied sugar's meaning is minted anew beside the copy
102	    door: Means,
103	    // the copy of each source expression reached so far, by its index: a node
104	    // the source reaches twice is one node in the copy. A cell, because it is
105	    // an identity — a walk that copies the rebuilder shares it.
106	    copies: Cell<List<ExprId?>>,
107	    // the mark every name a sugar's template BINDS gains, at its binder
108	    // and its reads, so none meets a name of the code it lands in; a name
109	    // the template reads and never binds is its home's and keeps itself,
110	    // as does one that comes through a hole. Absent for a copy that keeps
111	    // its names.
112	    fresh: string? = null,
113	    // the names the template binds, which `fresh` marks
114	    binds: List<string> = [],
115	}

117	/// A classifying walk over a store's quote body, `runs` the run mark
118	/// of each hole by index (`store.is_run_hole` over its fill
119	/// expression).
120	/// The nodes a copy made from its template, each keeping the template's span: those whose names
121	/// read there and those whose names came through a hole, never what a fill built at its own; the
122	/// expressions a hole named or filled apart, since their names read where the copy lands; and each
123	/// statement's seats whose names a hole filled.
124	export type CopiedNodes = { exprs: List<ExprId>, holed_exprs: List<ExprId>, stmts: List<StmtId>, pats: List<PatId>, params: List<ParamId>, landed: List<LandedAt> }

126	/// A copied statement's name seats a hole filled.
127	export type LandedAt = { stmt: StmtId, seats: List<LandedSeat> }

129	impl Rebuilder {
130	    fn made_nodes() -> CopiedNodes {
131	        CopiedNodes {
132	            exprs: self.made_exprs,
133	            holed_exprs: self.holed_exprs,
134	            stmts: self.made_stmts.concat(self.holed_stmts),
135	            pats: self.made_pats.concat(self.holed_pats),
136	            params: self.made_params,
137	            landed: [l with { seats: if self.holed_stmts.contains(l.stmt) { l.seats.concat([LandedSeat.Names]) } else { l.seats } } for l in self.landed]
138	                .concat(
139	                    [LandedAt { stmt: s, seats: [LandedSeat.Names] } for s in self.holed_stmts if !self.landed.any(it.stmt == s)],
140	                ),
141	        }
142	    }
143	}

217	/// A quote's holes classified — the kind of each, by its index.
218	export fn hole_kinds(store: SyntaxArena, e: ExprId) -> List<HoleKind> {
219	    let bp? = store.expr(e).body_of() else { return [] }
220	    match bp.view {
221	        .Verbatim(ss, arms) -> {
222	            mut rb = classifier(store, hole_runs(store, e))
223	            let _ = rb.stmts(ss)
224	            let _ = rb.arms(arms)
225	            rb.kinds
226	        },

228	        .Expanded(_) -> [],

232	/// What a quote's body PARSED as.
233	export fn quote_kind(store: SyntaxArena, e: ExprId) -> QuoteKind {
234	    let bp? = store.expr(e).body_of() else { return QuoteKind.Stmts }

content.text: The lead chose (A). The provider's own `check` judges its quote bodies, holes unfilled, for what they can say. message.content: Lead: your premise post didn't reach me in full, but from your options, (A). A provider's own `check` judges its quote bodies, since it wrote them: a refusal inside a template is the provider's error, spoken where the provider's author can fix it, once, not in every dependent. Downstream skips template-only items, per the ruling. The three witnesses move to checking the provider package (each red before, green after), plus one case showing a dependent no longer repeats the provider's template error. (B)'s shared judgment becomes unnecessary, and (C) pins nothing. A quote body that can't be judged standalone (its holes unfilled) is judged for what it can say, and its unfillable parts stay the instance's.

content.text: Before applying the ruling I'll check one premise: where does `generated_fn_body_judged`'s template actually live?

message.content:
Lead ruling, the line between the two: a finding inside generated code belongs to whoever WROTE the code it sits in. It's the same law as the dependency-warnings scope defects just landed (a check reports what the checked package wrote). So:
- template code from ANOTHER package, holding none of the checked package's writing: that package's own check judges it, and yours skips it. This is laws-fusion's cut, at the package line, not the file line.
- template code from the SAME package (your generated_fn_body_judged, with the template in a sibling file): judged, homed at the template, because the package wrote it.
- a generated item mixing the user's splices with a dependency's template: judged, with findings kept only at nodes the checked package wrote.
This keeps your witness green and buys back most of the +23%. Measure as you planned.

content.content:
# To false-refusals: witnesses and a cost lesson for generated bodies meeting the laws

From avra-lane-laws-fusion. The Lead held my parallel mechanism (9aab4462, 10ab1f8c, 3e209abf on
land57) out of batch 57 in favour of your general one (a59ef7dd). These are what it should pass and
what it should not cost.

## Witnesses: features/annotations/tests/rules_test.av, on the layer
Three cases the old path refuses and the layer (land57) says nothing about. Each wants exactly one
diagnostic (`refused_in` counts one), at the annotation:
1. "a rule the field cannot take / is refused at the annotation, once": `@long(3)` on `n: int`
   (`long(v: string, …)`). Old path: `type.mismatch` "argument 1 of `long` wants `string`, found
   `int`", at `main.av:5:12]`.
2. "a bounded rule on a type outside its bound is refused at the annotation": `@fits(3)` on `n: int`,
   `fits<T: Sized>`. Old path: `type.mismatch` "`int` does not implement `Sized`", at `main.av:7:12]`.
3. "a misspelled rule is refused at the annotation": `@lnog(3)`. Old path: `resolve.unresolved` "no
   `fn lnog` is defined", at `main.av:5:12]`.
The fourth pinned case ("a declaring annotation standing in its own file is refused by name")
already passes at land57.
The program's entry is `0`, so the generated `checked()` is never called. It must be judged
unreached: reach doesn't help, and a reached call (`R { n: 2 }.checked()`) was silent on land57 too.
With my mechanism: rules_test 8/8, features/annotations 183/183, and findings cmp-identical to
land57 for std-program, std-avrac and cli. So refusing these adds no finding to real code.

## What the facts look like (probed with AVRA_QTRACE)
- The generated item sits at `item_count + k`. Its impls are `file_impls(engine, file)[made_at]`,
  never `item_impls` (which reads only written text). Bodies via `typed_impl_bodies`.
- A refused node that came from the annotation's argument carries `ForeignOrigin { path:
  "app:src/main.av" (= template_home(file)), spanned_home: true }`. Its span is FILE-absolute
  (offset 160 for case 1), so it is placed by subtracting the written item's `item_start`.
- The template's own nodes carry the provider's origin. My rule: count a refusal or unread name only
  where the node is the file's own writing (path == template_home(file) && spanned_home). Unread names
  spliced here are `written_here: true`.
Your homing at the template must still land these three at the annotation in the user's file, not in
the provider's template.

## The cost lesson: +23% -> +2% (cli `tapes --findings`, cold, same-run pairs, fair gen-2 builds)
- First draft: per written item, scan `generator_sites(file)` and ask `site_generated` per site to
  find "which generated items did my sites make". cli 99.0/102.5 s -> 123.0/125.2 s (+23%).
  AVRA_QUERY_TIMES: item_refusals own 1.4 s -> 20.9 s; method_body_typed only +1.3 s. The cost was
  the per-item rescan, not the typing.
- Fix 1, `made_by`: one @query per file answering the site item of each generated item, in the order
  made (`MadeBy { sites: List<int> }`, flattened over generator_sites). +23% -> +4.3%
  (103.4 -> 107.8 s).
- Fix 2, skip by splice: a generated item whose store holds no node of the file's own writing
  (none with origin path == template_home && spanned_home) can say nothing in the file, so its bodies
  are not typed for this. Derives that splice nothing their site was handed (most `@derive(Saved)`)
  drop out. +4.3% -> +2% (99.0/100.4 -> 101.0/102.4 s); findings identical.
- If your mechanism walks every generated item through every law, the same shape applies: find each
  generated item's site once per file, and don't type what can't speak here. Keep both or measure
  past them.

## Where my code is, if useful
avra-lane-laws-fusion at 3e209abf (bundle land57..3e209abf, held out of batch 57):
packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/item_refused.av: `spliced_bodies`, `made_by`, `made_impls`,
`spelled_here`, `spells_here`, `moved_from`.

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS BUILD: exact retain/release/list-write counts, and the
# callers that cause them. Counting costs ~8% of a run, so it never
# ships: a census compiler is built BESIDE build/avra, from a runtime
# compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, and the shipping runtime library is
# rebuilt on every exit.
#   sh tools/census.sh check packages/std-avrac
#
# THE SHIPPING COMPILER IS NEVER REMOVED. It builds the census
# compiler, so a census that deletes it first has nothing to build
# with, and every recovery that rebuilds needs the memory and disk the
# census run just spent.
#
# CENSUS_EDIT MEASURES A WARM EDIT: the command runs once cold to fill the store,
# then CENSUS_EDIT edits the tree, and only the run after it is counted.
#   CENSUS_EDIT='sh tools/db_measure/edit_literal.sh' sh tools/census.sh check packages/cli
#
# A CENSUS THAT PRINTS NO COUNTS FAILS. A check that examined nothing
# is not a check that passed: no `rc:` line means the binary carried no
# census, and the run exits 1 saying so.
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.avra-cache"
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
: "${LLVM_PREFIX:=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm}"
export LLVM_PREFIX

# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK, under a memory cap: the old path's check the net runs
#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

i3 is building in the background now, with three fixes in. Nothing is committed yet.

- **`refuses_in_wrapped_body`:** findings in a generated item are homed by whoever wrote the narrowest node holding them. A finding on code the program wrote is left to the written item. Before, it went to the template whenever the numbers happened to fall inside a template node. This also merges the duplicated comprehension in `law_findings.av` that the idioms check flagged.
- **The 3 formats reds:** a generated item now records the item its generator stood on. If that item already fails its build, the generated item isn't judged. The case was a duplicated `grammar G`, which was refused once and then said four more cascade refusals from its generated door.
- **The unparsed template and the defect voice:** carried from before. A template whose file didn't parse is not copied, and lowering's catch-all is now a `language.defect` voice.

When the build finishes, I'll re-probe the grammar case in-process. Then I'll pin `template_unparsed_said_once` and check it's red on base, rerun the item-2 cases and `refuses_in_wrapped_body`, and start the full receipts.

[package]
name        = "@std/avrac"
version     = "0.0.1"
description = "Avra compiler library"

[lib]
name = "std-avrac"
path = "src/avrac.av"

# THE HOST SEAM's other half: language/llvm_api.av declares the C
# binding's prototypes; these keep the promise at link time. The
# prefix comes from the environment, so no machine's paths live in
# the tree — `LLVM_PREFIX` is what the Makefile passes.
[link]
# ffi.o is the EXTERN HOST's frame — the evaluator's way to call a
# linked C function by name. It is the COMPILER's C and rides here so
# that it never reaches a user's binary: every program the compiler
# emits links the runtime library, and a symbol resolver there would ship
# inside all of them.
objects = ["../../build/llvm_wrapper.o", "../../build/ffi.o"]
# ffi.o resolves the running image's own symbols by name, so a program
# linking this package keeps every symbol in its dynamic table.
dynamic_symbols = true
# LLVM IS LINKED STATICALLY (docs/2026_10_18_STATIC_LLVM.md): a shared libLLVM
# costs every command ~15 ms of relocation before it runs a line, and the
# compiler stays one binary. The libraries are the components the wrapper
# needs, in `llvm-config --link-static`'s order — AArch64 and WebAssembly
# beside X86, so one list serves both hosts; `tools/llvm_link.py --check`
# holds it to llvm-config and the hand-written clang lines read it from
# here. The C++ runtime is the platform's, named by AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME (`stdc++`
# on Linux, `c++` on macOS; the image, the Sprites, the shim and the Makefile
# set it); AVRA_SYS_SEARCH adds the directory the system's zstd lives in where
# it is off the default path.
search  = ["${LLVM_PREFIX}/lib", "${AVRA_SYS_SEARCH}"]
# A build that links shared names the one library standing for every one below.
shared  = "LLVM"
libs    = [
    "LLVMAArch64Disassembler",
    "LLVMAArch64AsmParser",
    "LLVMAArch64CodeGen",
    "LLVMAArch64Desc",
    "LLVMAArch64Utils",
    "LLVMAArch64Info",
    "LLVMWebAssemblyDisassembler",
    "LLVMWebAssemblyAsmParser",
    "LLVMWebAssemblyCodeGen",
    "LLVMWebAssemblyUtils",
    "LLVMWebAssemblyDesc",
    "LLVMWebAssemblyInfo",
    "LLVMX86TargetMCA",
    "LLVMMCA",
    "LLVMX86Disassembler",
    "LLVMX86AsmParser",
    "LLVMX86CodeGen",
    "LLVMX86Desc",
    "LLVMX86Info",
    "LLVMMCDisassembler",
    "LLVMAsmPrinter",
    "LLVMPasses",
    "LLVMIRPrinter",
    "LLVMHipStdPar",
    "LLVMCoroutines",
    "LLVMipo",
    "LLVMInstrumentation",
    "LLVMVectorize",
    "LLVMSandboxIR",
    "LLVMFrontendOpenMP",
    "LLVMFrontendDirective",
    "LLVMFrontendAtomic",
    "LLVMFrontendOffloading",

[package]
name        = "@std/avrac"
version     = "0.0.1"
description = "Avra compiler library"

[lib]
name = "std-avrac"
path = "src/avrac.av"

# THE HOST SEAM's other half: language/llvm_api.av declares the C
# binding's prototypes; these keep the promise at link time. The
# prefix comes from the environment, so no machine's paths live in
# the tree — `LLVM_PREFIX` is what the Makefile passes.
[link]
# ffi.o is the EXTERN HOST's frame — the evaluator's way to call a
# linked C function by name. It is the COMPILER's C and rides here so
# that it never reaches a user's binary: every program the compiler
# emits links the runtime library, and a symbol resolver there would ship
# inside all of them.
objects = ["../../build/llvm_wrapper.o", "../../build/ffi.o"]
# ffi.o resolves the running image's own symbols by name, so a program
# linking this package keeps every symbol in its dynamic table.
dynamic_symbols = true
# LLVM IS LINKED STATICALLY (docs/2026_10_18_STATIC_LLVM.md): a shared libLLVM
# costs every command ~15 ms of relocation before it runs a line, and the
# compiler stays one binary. The libraries are the components the wrapper
# needs, in `llvm-config --link-static`'s order — AArch64 and WebAssembly
# beside X86, so one list serves both hosts; `tools/llvm_link.py --check`
# holds it to llvm-config and the hand-written clang lines read it from
# here. The C++ runtime is the platform's, named by AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME (`stdc++`
# on Linux, `c++` on macOS; the image, the Sprites, the shim and the Makefile
# set it); AVRA_SYS_SEARCH adds the directory the system's zstd lives in where
# it is off the default path.
search  = ["${LLVM_PREFIX}/lib", "${AVRA_SYS_SEARCH}"]
# A build that links shared names the one library standing for every one below.
shared  = "LLVM"

   - **Paths.** The program layer is the default; `AVRA_PROGRAM=0` selects the old path. `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0` runs the layer alone. The net yields `NetSaid` (Off, Accepted, Refused, Unjudged); `net_stops` steps aside when the program uses forms only the layer builds.
   - **Ids.** `every_item_id` gives written ids, then `generated_id(k) = GENERATED_FIRST (2^40) + k`. `generated_rank(at)` is positional: 8 call sites, in item_generated, law_findings and item_methods. Written ids are keyed: `item_id_of(key, nth)` and `item_ids_of`.
   - **Sites.** `annotated_sites` covers written declarations only (by design: "a site never asks what generators make"). `declared_sites` can read a non-held (generated) item via `read_item`.
   - **Generated item shape.** `GeneratedItems { items, said, problems }`; `KeptProblem` carries the flags unread_home, unrun, trapped and unplaced. `file_generated` is a @cut_query. `site_generated` → `generated` @query, keyed by declaration meaning.

   - **Defects.** `defect_at(loc, message)` makes a Diag of kind `language.defect` (diagnostics/mod.av).
   - **Rendering.** `render_among(d, sources)`; `located_files(d)`.

message.content: Lead: good step. Fix the found one before rounds, since it's the same mechanism one pass over: a copy of a template whose file didn't parse must not be lowered either, exactly as it isn't judged. `build` then says only that file's parse refusal, as `check` does. Lowering's catch-all "a seat refuses a value here, in a body no law reads yet" firing means a body reached lowering that no law read. Add an assertion there: a body that reaches lowering has been judged. Make it a defect voice, so the next such path is loud. Witness: the unparsed-template case says the same under build and check. Then rounds.

Item 2's first step, generated bodies judged by the laws, is committed as a59ef7dd on the worktree branch, with receipts now running there. I'll design rounds while they run, without editing that tree.

<to_controller>Item 2, step 1: a59ef7dd on avra-lane-false-refusals-i2 (on top of 114b20a8). Receipts are running now; bundle after them.
- Laws over bodies walk every item, written and generated. A finding in a copy is homed at the template, at the template's own span; check and build render each frame over the file it names.
- Typing a method body now reads a generated item's impls; before, methods inside a generated `impl` were never typed.
- New layer law resolve.hole_bound, sharing one voice with the old path. Its witness package holds its own generator (the witness manifest takes no dependencies).

# The program layer's refusal suite

Each directory here is a package of its own, one case: a source the program layer must refuse
in the old path's words, or must build. `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh` judges them all;
its head says what each file means. In short:

- `refuses.expected`: the old path's `avra check` words, its warnings aside, paths as `<case>`.
  Both the old `check` and `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 avra build` exit 1 saying exactly this.
- `prints.expected`: what the product prints. The old `check` exits 0, the program layer builds
  the package, and its binary prints exactly this.
- `differs.why`: the paths are known to differ here, for the reason on its first line. The case
  is said and not failed while it differs, and fails once it holds until the file goes.
  `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known` lists them.

A new case is a directory with `avra.toml` and `src/main.av`; `PIN=1 sh
tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <case>` gives it the old path's expectation.

WHY HERE AND NOT UNDER A PACKAGE'S `src/`: `avra test` builds every package nested under a
package's sources as a suite of its own (`nested_roots` in compiler/suite.av), so a case that must
be refused would fail that package's tests. Under `tools/` no suite reaches them, as with
`tools/wasm-refuses/`.

# A refused pronoun in a derive's own file is never said

`it` binds to the nearest method call, so `fields.any(self.knows(it.name))` hands `it` to
`self.knows`, and is refused (`type.lambda`, `type.mismatch`). In a derive's own package that
refusal is never spoken:

1. `lib/` (a package whose trait `Shown` derives over its own `Part`): `avra check lib` on base56
   (a73903d2, gen-2) — the program layer: `file_generated (… parts.av) was asked while it was being
   answered, under … generator_print -> body_facts -> lowered_method_under -> method_body_typed ->
   package_generated_impls`. The old path (`AVRA_PROGRAM=0`) speaks the refusal. Fix the lambda
   (`(f) -> self.knows(f.name)`) and both check clean. `avra check .` (the root package, a user
   of `lib`) cycles the same way on the program layer, and speaks the refusal on the old path.
   The trigger is the derive running over a type in its OWN package: drop `lib/src/parts.av`
   and both paths speak the refusal.

2. The old path's trap needs std-ui's shape: apply `std-ui-view.patch` to std-ui (tree/view.av, at
   lane commit ff6593fb or later — one line, `self.kept_state(it)` inside `t.fields.find(…)`), then
   `AVRA_PROGRAM=0 avra run std-ui-driver` → `avra: index 1 is out of bounds (length 1)`, and the
   program layer → `generator_print (@std/ui src/tree/view.av ! View) was asked while it was being
   answered`. Without the patch the driver says only its own interp_hole refusal.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Bash, Edit, Monitor, Read, ReadNotifications, ToolSearch</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - The controller/lead lane is `avra-lane-false-refusals`, working in /work/avra.
   - Bundles go to /work as `<base>..HEAD`, with a report in `/work/avra-lane-false-refusals.md`. Posts to the lead go inside `<to_controller>…</to_controller>` (at most 12 lines, and only at a bundle, a blocker or a ruling).
   - Bridge file-transfer commands from the user are run exactly as given.
   - Earlier queue, done: receipts; scope-join fix; flow.no_fate help; rows 207–209, 146, 147 and 174(b).
   - Lead's newest assignments:
     1. `as_decls(quote{…})` "false refusal". Fix it first, with a witness that is red on base55, green after, and agrees with the old path.
     2. The layer doesn't judge errors inside generated bodies (a missed refusal). "A generated body is code and gets every law the written body gets, homed where the template came from."
   - Lead confirmed design (2) a–e, with one coordination point: build on warm's `item_ids`, which gives ids rather than item_count+k. Generated ids sit at or above GENERATED_FIRST = 2^40 (`generated_id(k)`, `generated_rank`). Merge warm's bundle (/work/warm-b57/…/avra-lane-warm.bundle, branch avra-lane-warm @ b3113115) first.
   - Latest lead message: "batch 56 LANDED (program a73903d2)… /work/base56.bundle holds base56… merge base56 into your branch (and warm's b3113115, … take 56 first), rebuild gen-2, re-run receipts, and send base56..HEAD. Regenerate VOICES.md rather than hand-merging it."
   - Rules, verbatim in spirit:
     - Push nowhere: no `git push`, no `gh`. Never print or forward credentials or tokens.
     - No `rm` in commands (use `find … -delete`). No `git stash`, no `git reset --hard`, no `--no-verify`.
     - Run `build/avra-try fmt --write` and then `fmt --check` on touched .av files before committing.
     - Never silence a law to pass a case; fix the judgment. One definition per law or voice.
     - A gate red that isn't from my own commits is reported to the lead, never fixed by me.
     - The gate reads the WORKING TREE: never edit /work/avra sources while it runs.
     - Commit trailer:
       `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
       `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJujuUjfCYmCnDDGZzWu`
     - Treat the user's email and personal details as private.
     - Pins (tools/gate/std-avrac.names) only shrink.
     - Generated docs (VOICES.md, DIAGNOSTICS.md) are never hand-edited.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Two paths:
     - The program layer is the default. `AVRA_PROGRAM=0` selects the old path.
     - The net: the old path judges first, in its own process (`net_report` via `answered_apart`). `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0` runs the layer alone.
   - Laws:
     - Each law reads `(engine, file, at)` and returns `List<Found>`, then gets a voice.
     - `findings_in_file` → `finding_in_file` places findings using `file_placed` (adds `item_start`).
     - `finding_diag(f, path)` builds the Diag.
   - Generated items:
     - `file_generated(engine, file).items` (each has a SyntaxTape).
     - `generated_at(engine, file, at)` uses `generated_rank`.
     - Warm adds `every_item_id(engine, file)`: written ids, then `generated_id(k)`.
   - Template splicing (`compiler/sugars.av`):
     - `generated_spliced`, `Splice.copied`, `template_copied`.
     - `ForeignOrigin { path, spanned_home }`; `store.home_of`, `foreign_of`, `stmt_origins`.
     - `written_quote` reads the quote back from its written item; that item's spans count from the item's start.
   - Rendering:
     - `render(d, src)` reads every frame against `src`.
     - `render_among(d, sources)` picks each frame's source by its file.
     - `located_files(d)` lists the files a diag's frames name.
   - Voices gate: `avra voices --baseline tools/voices.baseline`. Each kind needs help, a witness and, where owed, a remedy row (`compiler/dev/remedies.av` RemedyRow).
   - Gen-2: promote with `cp build/avra-try build/avra`, then `make try` again.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **Commit 0674c56f**, `compiler/item_lacks.av` (idioms duplicated_literal fix).
     - `lacked_declared` → `records_lacking(engine, file, at, (l, _j) -> [x.name for x in record_signature(engine, file, l.name)?.fields ?? []])`.
     - `lacked_twice` → `records_lacking(engine, file, at, (l, j) -> l.fields.take(j))`.
     - New: `fn records_lacking(engine, file, at, refused: fn(Lacking, int) -> List<string>) -> List<Found> { [Found { at: l.at, args: [l.name, f] } for l in lacking_at(...) if l.kind == ItemKind.Record for j, f in l.fields if refused(l, j).contains(f)] }`.
     - Bundle 2: base55..0674c56f, uploaded through the bridge.
   - **Commit de20a661**, `packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av`.
     - `NetSaid` gains `Unjudged`: "no verdict… vouches for nothing".
     - `net_report` now returns `NetSaid`: `.Answered` gives Refused or Accepted; `.Ended`/`.Outlasted` gives `NetSaid.Unjudged` and appends the note to net-verdict.err.
     - `net_said` loop:
       `mut said = NetSaid.Accepted; for p in paths { let one = net_report(p, judge); if one is .Refused { return one }; if one is .Unjudged { said = one } }; said`
     - `net_vouches` is unchanged (`said is .Accepted`).
     - New case `tools/program-refusals/quote_handed_to_as_decls/`:
       - avra.toml, src/main.av (`@derive(Nowhere)` over `type P`, then `gone()`), vendor/prov (provider with `source: as_decls(quote { fn gone() -> int { 40 + 2 } })`).
       - refuses.expected: type.mismatch at `<case>/vendor/prov/src/prov.av:9:40`.
       - differs.why: the old path traps (index 0 out of bounds).
     - Witness: the pre-fix binary (build/avra-try.pre-net) printed the false-refusal header; after the fix only the mismatch appears. In a plain package both paths say type.mismatch.
   - **Merge 46046705** (base56 into de20a661, on temporary branch fr-remerge).
     - item_generated.av import: `use @std.meta.{Diagnostic, Directive, Node, derive}` (base56 dropped budgets_of).
     - item_refused.av: took base56's lists (which add `.Heard(_)`) and inserted `.Capacity(_) or ` after `.CompBound(_) or ` on 18 lines.
     - std-avrac.names: kept base56's lines minus pins my side removed (191 pins; no additions).
     - docs/VOICES.md regenerated with `build/avra-try voices --report`.
   - **Commit 17efc5e8**, `compiler/dev/remedies.av`.
     - RemedyRow `annotation.template_unread`, says "is no file this program reads".
     - refused = provided_program(… `as_decls(template("@x/gone:src/gone.av", 0, ["fn gone() {}"], []))`).
     - applied = provider with `source: quote { fn gone() {} }`; becomes Then.Clean.
     - remedies_test 7/7. The voices NEW gaps are back to base55's 7.
   - **Merge fdcb7f0e** (avra-lane-warm).
     - Conflicts in item_bound_calls, item_generic_methods, item_methods_twice and item_misnamed: kept base56's `file_found_by(...)` bodies.
     - Converted base56's new `0..item_count` loops to `item_ids`: law_findings.av `file_found_by`, testing/held.av:768 (import item_count→item_ids), item_expanded.av:31.
     - Branch `avra-lane-false-refusals` now points at fdcb7f0e. The old warm-first merge is kept as `avra-lane-false-refusals-premerge`; fr-remerge was deleted.
     - Gen-2 built (old binary saved as build/avra.pre56); VOICES.md matches.
   - **Item-2 WIP**, in worktree /work/avra-i2 (branch avra-lane-false-refusals-i2 from fdcb7f0e). /work/q3run/item2-wip.patch applied cleanly; the edits below are uncommitted and unbuilt.
     - `compiler/item_said.av`:
       - `use core.{some_list, template_file}`.
       - `ProgramFile = { file, full, elsewhere: fn(SourceFileAddress) -> string = spelled_file }`.
       - `file_law_diags` iterates `every_item_id(engine, h.file)` and uses `finding_diag(f, finding_path(h, f))`.
       - `finding_path`: if `f.home` is set, `template_file(home)` → `(h.elsewhere)(file)`; otherwise `h.full`.
     - `compiler/law_findings.av`:
       - `file_erring` uses `every_item_id`.
       - LawFinding gets `home: string? = null`.
       - `finding_in_file`: `if generated_rank(at) != null { return made_finding(read_item(engine, file, at).store, f) }`.
       - `made_finding(store, f)`: homes the finding at the narrowest template-written node holding its place (`template_home_at`, which scans exprs and stmts with `spanned_home` origins, sorted by width), keeps template places, and drops fixes and aside. With no home, the place is null.
       - `type Homed = { path, span }`.
       - Imports added: ExprId, StmtId, SyntaxArena.
     - `compiler/item_generated.av`:
       - `export fn item_stands(engine, file, at) -> bool { item_held(...) || generated_at(...) != null }`.
       - `written_quote` returns `Scratch { store, body: q, start: item_start(engine, file, i) }`.
     - `compiler/item_refused.av`: `item_refusals` guard uses `item_stands` (doc: "written or generated").
     - `cli/src/commands/check_program.av`:
       - `erring_said` builds `sources = [new_source_file(p, text_at(p) ?? "") for p in distinct([h.full].concat(flatten([located_files(d) for d in found])))]` and uses `render_among`.
       - `same_said` also compares `primary.loc?.file`.
       - Imports: `distinct, flatten`; `located_files, render_among`.
     - `cli/src/commands/tapes.av` `program_file`: `elsewhere: (o) -> disk.on_disk(o.package_name, o.path_in_package)`.
     - `testing/held.av` `named`: `elsewhere: (o: SourceFileAddress) -> self.named(o).full`.
     - New in the worktree, for precise spans:
       - `core/store.av`: method `moved_on(exprs, stmts, pats, params, by)` shifts spans with plain for/let/if loops (`place_expr`, `stmts.place`, `pat_spans.set_at`, `param_spans.set_at`); top-level `fn moved_span(span, by) -> Span`.
       - `compiler/sugars.av`:
         - `Scratch` gets `start: int? = null`; `TemplateCopy` gets `placed: bool = false`.
         - In `template_copied`, after `note_made`: `let start = if origin.spanned_home { s.start } else { null }`; when set, `store.moved_on(rb.made_exprs, rb.made_stmts, rb.made_pats, rb.made_params, start!)`; the copy returns `placed: start != null` and `exprs` holed-only when placed.
         - In `Splice.copied`: `if !copy.placed { for s in copy.stmts { …place(s.index, site) } }`.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Idioms 1 on c4aa476f (2 NEW duplicated_literal in item_lacks): fixed in 0674c56f; idioms then 0.
   - lacks_test shows 6 failures: all are pins 217–222 (reads of a lacked field), not mine.
   - The "as_decls false refusal" was really a net mislabel: the old path traps, the net took that as acceptance. Fixed with Unjudged.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Item-2 witness, /work/q3run/r174/read_bad (template `fn gone() -> int { "no" }`). The old path says:
     `error[type.mismatch]: the body answers `string` but `gone` declares `int`` at prov.av:4:91, label "this is `string`", help "the body's last expression is the answer — make it a `int`, or change the declared answer".

++>>>>>>> base56
  features/fns — provided reads a file of the package into a kind / a call that names no kind / it refuses, saying the file's octets do not choose it
  features/lists — the comprehension planner / a declared lookup / a lookup whose seat does not wear the field's type is refused
  features/maps / a walk over a map — its entries, the prelude's / a scan by value says what the map holds
@@@ -219,12 -160,14 +165,10 @@@ features/structs (lacks) / a generic re

  features/structs (lacks) / a record lacking `secret` on purpose / a literal writing it refuses with the reason

usage: avra tapes [--program-only] [--signatures] [--left] [--core] [--lowered] [--program-runs] [--all-made] [--generators] [--built] [--entry-run] [--link-words] [--findings] [--new-only] [--law-witnesses] [--kinds] [--only <value>] [--budget <value>] [--args <value>] [--share <value>] [--first <value>] <file>

Read every file of a package off its item tapes and hold each to the parse

flags:
  --program-only   run the program layer alone over every file and say how long it took
  --signatures     hold every fn's signature to the workspace's too
  --left           with --signatures, --core, --lowered or --ran, show where what doesn't agree stands
  --core           elaborate every fn into the core its sugars mean, and hold each sugar's type to its meaning's
  --lowered        lower every fn the program layer can lower whole, and hold its IR to the workspace's
  --program-runs   run each program test under the directory through the program layer's lowering, in the evaluator and natively, and hold its output to its `.expected`
  --all-made       with --ran, fail when any program test is not made on the program layer yet, as well as when one fails
  --generators     make each generator the package's traits write on the program layer, with every body it reaches
  --built          walk every body the package's program reaches, past each not lowered yet, and tally what isn't made by why
  --entry-run      build the package's program through the program layer natively, a body not lowered yet trapping by name where it's reached, and run it with --args
  --link-words     say whether the package's link line read off the manifests is the one a workspace says
  --findings       say what every law, then every rule that reads syntax alone, finds in each file the package's program reads, rendered as `check` renders it
  --new-only       say each form only the program layer builds that the package's program uses, one per line: what the old path is never asked to judge
  --law-witnesses  write each law's witness under the directory as a package of its own, named by the law
  --kinds          say every kind of finding the program layer holds, one per line, sorted

options:
  --only <value>    hold only the package's files whose path starts with this (`src/compiler/`)
  --budget <value>  with --built, stop the walk after this many seconds and tally what it reached
  --args <value>    with --run-entry, the arguments the program runs with, split on spaces
  --share <value>   lower the share `<core>/<of>` of declared bodies a worked-ahead build hands one process, here, in its order
  --first <value>   ask the lowering of the fn `<path> <name>` before anything else, and say what it answered

args:
  file  the source file

#!/bin/sh
# THE PROGRAM LAYER REFUSES WHAT THE OLD PATH REFUSES, IN ITS WORDS, AND BUILDS WHAT IT BUILDS.
# Each case under tools/program-refusals/ is a package of its own:
#   refuses.expected — the source must be refused: the old path's `check` and the program
#     layer's `build` each exit 1, and what each says, its warnings aside, is exactly this text;
#   prints.expected — the source must not be refused: the old path's `check` exits 0, the
#     program layer builds it, and what the product prints is exactly this text;
#   target — a case for another target, its triple: each path BUILDS it for that target, the build's
#     refusal is its words, and a printing case's module runs under node (`tools/run_wasm.mjs`); on a
#     machine with no toolchain for the target, both paths refuse in the toolchain's same words, exit 2,
#     and the case is said untooled, neither held nor failed;
#   warns.expected — beside either: each path's warnings, their first lines in the order said, are
#     exactly this text (for a case only the program layer builds, that layer's warnings); an
#     empty one says no warning is said;
#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cases_dir="$root/tools/program-refusals"
# the node a wasm case's module runs under: NODE, else /opt/node24's, else the PATH's
node=${NODE:-$( [ -x /opt/node24/bin/node ] && echo /opt/node24/bin/node || echo node )}

. "$root/tools/lib/cases.sh"
# every case, by name
cases() { cases_in "$cases_dir"; }

if [ "${1:-}" = --cases ]; then
    cases
    exit 0
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = --known ]; then
    n=0
    for name in $(cases); do
        [ -e "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why" ] || continue
        echo "$name: $(head -1 "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why")"
        n=$((n + 1))
    done
    echo "witness_program_refusal: $n of $(cases | wc -l | tr -d ' ') cases known to differ"
    exit 0
fi
avra=${1:-build/avra-try}
case $avra in /*) ;; *) avra="$root/$avra" ;; esac
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_refusal: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
tmp=$(mktemp -d)

#   target — a case for another target, its triple: each path BUILDS it for that target, the build's
#     refusal is its words, and a printing case's module runs under node (`tools/run_wasm.mjs`); on a
#     machine with no toolchain for the target, both paths refuse in the toolchain's same words, exit 2,
#     and the case is said untooled, neither held nor failed;
#   warns.expected — beside either: each path's warnings, their first lines in the order said, are
#     exactly this text (for a case only the program layer builds, that layer's warnings); an
#     empty one says no warning is said;
#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cases_dir="$root/tools/program-refusals"
# the node a wasm case's module runs under: NODE, else /opt/node24's, else the PATH's
node=${NODE:-$( [ -x /opt/node24/bin/node ] && echo /opt/node24/bin/node || echo node )}

. "$root/tools/lib/cases.sh"
# every case, by name
cases() { cases_in "$cases_dir"; }

if [ "${1:-}" = --cases ]; then
    cases
    exit 0
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = --known ]; then
    n=0
    for name in $(cases); do
        [ -e "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why" ] || continue
        echo "$name: $(head -1 "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why")"
        n=$((n + 1))
    done
    echo "witness_program_refusal: $n of $(cases | wc -l | tr -d ' ') cases known to differ"
    exit 0
fi
avra=${1:-build/avra-try}
case $avra in /*) ;; *) avra="$root/$avra" ;; esac
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_refusal: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
tmp=$(mktemp -d)

#!/bin/sh
# The receipt run used for each bundle, as run in this lane. Usage: sh receipts.sh <base-ref> <log>
# Run from /work/avra after `source /etc/profile.d/avra.sh`. Never edit the tree while it runs.
base=${1:-batch53}; log=${2:-/tmp/receipts.log}
cd /work/avra || exit 1
make try > /dev/null 2>&1; echo "make try $? ($(git rev-parse --short HEAD))" > "$log"
build/avra fmt --check $(git diff --name-only "$base"..HEAD -- '*.av') | tail -1 >> "$log"
AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000 build/avra check packages/cli --baseline tools/idioms.baseline > /tmp/idioms.log 2>&1; echo "idioms $?" >> "$log"
for p in std-time std-task; do build/avra-try tapes packages/$p --program-runs > /tmp/runs-$p.log 2>&1; echo "runs $p: $(grep '^ran:' /tmp/runs-$p.log | cut -c1-200)" >> "$log"; done
for s in avrac-a avrac-b avrac-c avrac-d avrac-e avrac-f avrac-g; do sh tools/gate.sh $s > /tmp/gate-$s.log 2>&1; tail -1 /tmp/gate-$s.log >> "$log"; done
AVRA_PROGRAM=1 build/avra check packages/std-avrac > /tmp/check.log 2>&1; echo "check std-avrac exit $?" >> "$log"
AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 build/avra build packages/cli > /tmp/cli.log 2>&1; echo "cli $?" >> "$log"
sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra > /tmp/wref.log 2>&1; tail -1 /tmp/wref.log >> "$log"
sh tools/witness_program_runs.sh > /tmp/wruns.log 2>&1; echo "witness_program_runs $? $(tail -1 /tmp/wruns.log)" >> "$log"
echo done >> "$log"

# every store under the packages named emptied — a nested package's and a program test's too — so the
# rows after read them cold
cold() { for p in "$@"; do find "packages/$p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; done; return 0; }

# build/avra as HEAD's compiler: kept when it was built from this tree's compiler source, else made in
# ONE generation — from the committed seed's link where no compiler stands, else from the one that does
# — with the package libraries beside it, built without building the compiler again. A gate's
# compiler makes no claim of the net, so it is built without it; the two-generation fixed point is the
# build slice's.
compiler() {
    if compiler_stands; then return 0; fi
    if [ ! -x build/avra ]; then row compiler-recover make recover || return 1; fi
    row compiler-gen1 env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra || return 1
    row compiler-libs env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make -o avra libs
}

# what `$1`'s cold build of packages/cli took, in seconds, net on or off by `$2`
cli_built() {
    cold cli
    find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete
    c0=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-cold" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    c1=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-warm" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    echo "cli build net $1: cold $((c1 - c0))s, warm $(( $(date +%s) - c1 ))s" >>"$out/seconds"
    # the warm build's heir waited out, before a row after empties the store it saves
    env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
}

slice_build() {
    row try make try
    row avra-a make avra && cp build/avra "$out/avra-a"
    cold cli
    row avra-b make avra && { cmp -s build/avra "$out/avra-a"; judged fixed-point $?; }
    cli_built on 1

# WHAT EVERY VOICE CARRIES: a witness, help, and a structured fix where
# its registry row owes one — read from the registry and the compiler's
# own rendering of each witness (`avra voices`). A NEW kind or rule with
# a gap refuses; tools/voices.baseline lists the gaps that stand and only
# shrinks (`make voices-accept` prunes what a fix paid). docs/VOICES.md
# is the generated inventory, never edited.
voices:
	@./avra voices --baseline tools/voices.baseline
	@python3 tools/voices_spoken.py
	@./avra voices --report > build/VOICES.md.gen
	@cmp -s build/VOICES.md.gen docs/VOICES.md || { \
	  echo "voices: docs/VOICES.md is not what the compiler says — it is generated, never edited:"; \
	  echo "voices:   ./avra voices --report > docs/VOICES.md"; \
	  diff docs/VOICES.md build/VOICES.md.gen 2>/dev/null | head -30; exit 1; }

5. **A channel says how much it holds.** `0` hands over.
6. **Loss is spoken.** A dropping channel counts what it dropped.
7. **A `select` is exhaustive over ends.**
8. **Arms take turns.** A ready arm is passed over at most `arms − 1`
   times. `select in order { }` scans as written.
9. **A task answers once.** An arm over a task made outside the loop
   must leave the loop. A task made in an arm head and not taken is
   cancelled, never joined.
10. **A cancelled wait fails with `Cancelled`.** It travels to the
    scope that asked, which answers it. Anyone else watching the task
    gets it as a typed value with a trace (§5.4); no cancel is silent.
    A wake that already claimed a wait is honoured first.
----
heads → h0 … hn
loop:
    for i in rotation(cursor): if hi.ready() { v = hi.take(-1); arm i; leave }
    else-arm, if any → run it, leave
    for each live arm i: hi.arm(i)
    (a, m) = avra_wait_park()      // a = −1: cancelled (§5.4)
    if h_a is gate-claimed: v = h_a.take(m); arm a; leave
    goto loop
leave: every task made in an arm head and not taken is cancelled
```

TASKS IN ARM HEADS. A task made by an arm's expression belongs to the
`select`. Leaving the `select` cancels each one not taken (an offer is
retracted, a timer dropped). It is never joined. (v2 would have waited
out every unfired `quiet`.)

TIMERS, BY TYPE. `after(d)` answers `Deadline`; `quiet(d)` answers
`Quiet`. An arm whose head is a CALL answering `Deadline`, inside a
loop, is `flow.fresh_deadline`: it would restart every turn. `Quiet`
is the type that says so on purpose. The rule reads types, never names.
