# Handoff — lane `avra-lane-parity-false-refusals`

## Lane and scope

The Avra compiler's PROGRAM LAYER and its parity with the old path, in `/work/avra`, branch
`avra-lane-parity-false-refusals`. The lane owns false refusals and missing refusals between the
two paths, plus flow, tasks and channels engine defects (the lead assigned these to the lane).

Rules the lead set, kept verbatim in spirit:
- Push nowhere: no `git push` and no `gh`. Never print or forward a credential or token.
- No `rm` in commands (use `find … -delete`). No `git stash`, no `git reset --hard`, no `--no-verify`.
- Run `build/avra-try fmt --write <files>` on touched `.av` files before committing. The formatter
  sometimes needs a second pass; run `fmt --check` after it.
- Never silence a law to pass a case: fix the judgment. One definition per law or voice.
- A gate red that isn't from your own commits is REPORTED to the lead, never fixed by you.
- Post to the lead only at a bundle, a blocker or a ruling, in at most 12 lines.
- The gate reads the WORKING TREE: never edit sources while it runs.

## Base

- Branch is on **batch53** (`d5062c3274`, "Merge remote-tracking branch 'ui/r3' into program-land-53").
- **batch55** (`912fc732d7`) was fetched as ref `batch55`. It contains batch53 and NONE of the
  commits below. The lead says to base new work on the newest batch bundle, so rebase onto batch55
  next. Expect conflicts only in `tools/gate/std-avrac.names` and the Seating match lists in
  `compiler/item_refused.av`; resolve them as unions, as before.
- Each bundle's prerequisite is `d750dfa7`.

## Commits ahead of batch53 (oldest first), NOT yet sent to the lead

The lead is waiting for these as `batch53..HEAD`, for batch 54.

| sha | what |
|---|---|
| 31b50976b | program layer: a `collect enum E: T` names a trait, and every member implements it (2 laws; 4 pins removed) |
| 36395d0a8 | program layer: a `produce`/`channel` capacity that is no `int` says so in the old path's words (`Seating.Capacity`, law `capacity_mismatch`, voice `capacity_unint`; 1 pin removed) |
| 935e69727 | engine (a1): `avra_guard_run` is a cancel point (`waits: true`), so a cut `contained` body unwinds to its `within` |
| 5ab319d1a | std-task (d): `next()` takes a value left in `handed`, whoever's claim left it |
| 067134e8f | select (e): taking an arm cancels each task a head made that still runs; a list literal of spawns in a head counts as made there (layer `lowers.av` and old `lower.av`) |
| 1dd870e10 | engine (c, a2, b): the evaluator's tick obeys the shield; a caught trap ends the `within`s its body opened; evaluator guards are per task |

Program tests added in `packages/std-time/src/tests/`: `deferred_whole`, `contained_cut`,
`contained_trap_within`, `contained_interleaved`, `next_after_claim`, `select_head_cancelled`.

**Gate on 1dd870e1**, in `/tmp/claude-0/gate17.log`:
- PASS: `make try`, `fmt --check` (19 files, 0 differing), idioms 0 new.
- PASS: all 39 `std-time` and `std-task` program tests, in both evaluator and native.
- PASS: gate avrac-a to g, all 0 failed.
- PASS: `check std-avrac` exit 0, cli build (`AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0`) exit 0.
- NOT FINISHED when the budget ran out: `witness_program_refusal` and `witness_program_runs`.
  Re-run these two before sending, or the whole receipt set after the rebase onto batch55.

## In flight

Nothing is uncommitted; the tree was clean at handoff. Work investigated but not started:

**Scope-join fix**. Ruling: "nothing outlives its scope". Every task a scope made is joined at
each of that scope's exits, a normal end included, never only released.
- Cause, found by reading only: `features/block/lowers.av` has a shortcut. A block holding only its
  tail (`lead.is_empty()`) lowers the tail with no `opened()`/`closed()`. So `owns()` of a `select`
  head files its `Ending.Joined` in the body's BASE endings frame (`core/lowering.av:513`).
- That frame is ended only by unwinding exits (`unwound_exit`/`answer_exit` → `ended_from(0, …)`).
  The normal end in `compiler/item_lowered.av` `signed_lowered` (~line 313–320) only does
  `scope_exit(r)` and `RetVal(r)`. The task handle is merely released, and `avra_task_release`
  joins only if it holds the last handle, which a filed waiter can prevent.
- Planned fix: add a helper in `core/endings.av`, e.g. `body_ended(r)`, that ends frame 0's
  endings with `Leaving.Answering(r)` and clears it. Call it before `RetVal` in `signed_lowered`
  and in `core/closures.av` (after `if framed { body.closed() }`). Check the other
  `RetVal` sites in `compiler/item_lowered.av` (state, collect and enum bodies) and
  `core/dyn_boxes.av`.
- Repro: `/work/q3run/eprobe4` (a fn whose body is a lone `select`; `avra-try ir .` shows the
  normal exit has only `release`, no `avra_task_settle`) and `/work/q3run/eprobe3`.
- Then: add a program test that reads at once, with no 50 ms wait, passing in both engines. Remove
  the `sleep(ms(50))` in `std-time/src/tests/select_head_cancelled` once joins hold. Fix the
  wording in `docs/2026_10_05_CHANNELS.md` §5.2 (around line 733): replace "It is never joined"
  with "cancelled when the select is left, and joined by its scope like any task".

## Next 3 items, in order

1. Re-run the two witnesses on HEAD (or the full receipts). Bundle `batch53..HEAD`, send it with
   `send_files`, and post the receipts. If the lead now wants it on batch55, rebase first.
2. Rebase onto batch55. Do the scope-join fix above as its own commit, with a test and the docs
   wording.
3. On batch55, update the `flow.no_fate` help as its own small commit. The voice is `fate_unnamed`
   in `packages/std-avrac/src/features/components/check.av:287`; its help says
   ``name the letter a failed item is buried in — `dead: <sink>` ``. In batch55 (services slice
   17) the worker takes the letter queue itself, so change the help to the current form, e.g.
   `dead: undeliverable`, after checking the worker's `dead` field type in batch55's
   `std-queue/src/queue.av`. Also update its golden: the remedy row at
   `compiler/dev/remedies.av` ~602 (its `applied` writes `dead: "letter"`) and any spec asserting
   the help text.

After those, from the lead's earlier list: type.lacks (3 programs), type.embed_literal (1),
type.guard_value (1), language.defect (1). They are rows of `/work/package-245.tsv`: 207–209,
147, 146 and 174.

## Open rulings and asks

- RULED (e): cancel on leaving the select AND join at the enclosing scope. The CHANNELS 5.2
  wording is to be fixed (item 2 above).
- WITHDRAWN: `then` as a field name. Every path refuses it alike; drop it.
- Told to the lead, no action pending:
  - A collect-enum member declared in ANOTHER file than its enum (package scope) is refused at the
    enum, not at its own declaration: a law finding can't land in another file.
  - n13–n16 spec-harness `@std/task` stand-in problem, sent to the spec-harness lane via the lead.

## Things a fresh session would trip on

- Environment: `source /etc/profile.d/avra.sh` before builds.
- Build with `make try`, which produces `build/avra-try`; test with it. `build/avra` is the older
  binary the gate scripts use; it was last built at 01:24 and predates today's runtime changes.
- Gate and receipt commands, exactly as run (see `/work/handoff/receipts.sh`):
  - `sh tools/gate.sh avrac-a` … `avrac-g`
  - `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 build/avra check packages/std-avrac`
  - `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 build/avra build packages/cli`
  - `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra`
  - `sh tools/witness_program_runs.sh`
  - `AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000 build/avra check packages/cli --baseline tools/idioms.baseline`
    (idioms; must report 0 NEW)
  - `build/avra fmt --check $(git diff --name-only <base>..HEAD -- '*.av')`
  - Program tests: `build/avra-try tapes packages/std-time --program-runs [--only src/tests/<name>] [--left]`
- Pin list: `tools/gate/std-avrac.names` lists cases the layer fails. It ONLY SHRINKS: remove a pin
  when its case passes, and keep the header comments accurate.
- Probing a spec: write a temporary `zz_*_test.av` beside the tests (a `spec "…" { given … { then … } }`
  block). Old-path diagnostics come from
  `h.old_program(h.standing("app","src/main.av"))` → `flatten([a.diagnostics for a in p.files]).concat(p.voices).concat(p.defects)`;
  the layer's from `h.judged_at(path)`. Delete the probe afterwards with `find … -delete`.
- Scratch: `/work/q3run/` holds the repro copies and probes (`engine_repros/`, `eprobe*`).
  `/work/q3repro/engine_repros/` holds the reporter's originals, each with a `REPRO.txt`.
- Backup branches: `backup-pre45`, `backup-pre45c`, `backup-pre51`, `backup-pre53` (states before
  each rebase).
- Bridge: `mcp__claude-bridge__post_to_controller` and `send_files`. The new account will give a
  new session token.
- Commit trailer: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` plus the
  `Claude-Session` line for the new session.

1	# Avra — clean-room compiler
2	
3	## AVRA PRINCIPLES
4	
5	The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
6	Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
7	dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
8	feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.
9	
10	- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
11	- P2  substrate for autonomous services
12	- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
13	- P4  Rust-level performance or better
14	- P5  full-stack vertical integration
15	- P6  paradox collapse
16	- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
17	- P8  escape hatches everywhere
18	- P9  boundaries are contracts
19	- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
20	- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
21	- P12 one source of truth, many projections
22	- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
23	- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
24	- P17 composability over featurefulness
25	
26	Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
27	time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
28	LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
29	Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
30	and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
31	README.md).
32	
33	Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
34	- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
35	- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
36	- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape
37	
38	Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.
39	
40	## Comments
41	
42	Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
43	points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
44	Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
45	invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.
46	
47	## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn
48	
49	First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
50	the body exists, answer:
51	
52	1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
53	   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
54	2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
55	   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
56	   push-ceremony.
57	3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
58	   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
59	4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
60	   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
61	5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
62	   loop.
63	6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
64	   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
65	   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.
66	
67	DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
68	tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
69	sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
70	runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
71	gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
72	found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
73	only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
74	the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
75	table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
76	debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
77	time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
78	named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.
79	
80	## Style
81	
82	- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
83	  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
84	  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
85	  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
86	  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
87	  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
88	  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
89	- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
90	  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
91	  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
92	  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
93	  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
94	  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
95	  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
96	  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
97	  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
98	  standard signature and is not a verb.
99	- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
100	  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
101	  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
102	  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
103	  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
104	- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
105	  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
106	  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
107	  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
108	  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
109	  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
110	  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
111	  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
112	  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
113	  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
114	  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
115	  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
116	  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
117	- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
118	  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
119	  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
120	  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says
121	  so in its own words. A blanket "builder failed:" prefix once told
122	  the reader the compiler had broken about every law — five of the
123	  seven refusals sampled at c7b5038 — while `Cause` had separated
124	  `Builder` from `Defect` all along: the seam was right and only the
125	  WORDING lied. THE GENERAL SHAPE: A PARAPHRASE OF A FLAG IS A
126	  SECOND COPY, and the reader believes the words — the flag is
127	  checked by the code, the prose by nobody. So the WORDS carry the
128	  CLAIM and the STRUCTURE carries the CATEGORY (`Cause.Builder`
129	  projects to F0102, compiler/codes.av), and the words never restate
130	  the category.
131	- A projection is ONE match: nested patterns
132	  (`.Node(.NAlt(a)) -> a, _ -> null`), never an unwrap ladder.
133	- The third copy of a shape names the concept: shared walks and
134	  registries get ONE definition (`post_order`, `file_command`) and
135	  the copies die. Two copies may wait; three never do.
136	
137	## Dogfooding is design
138	
139	The compiler is Avra's first user. When its code WANTS a construct
140	the language lacks — a sugar, a projection, a rule — add the ask to
141	the ROADMAP's sugar backlog, naming the wanting site, as part of the
142	change that hit it. Request your own features: the backlog feeds the
143	spec. The same discipline runs one level down: a PATTERN discovered
144	while writing (a beautiful form, a smell, a licensed exception) is
145	an IDIOM — it lands in DOGFOODING.md's registry at discovery, and
146	the greppable ones become `rule` declarations `avra check` finds
147	directly (compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av). The
148	registry is the idiom engine's spec, written by dogfooding.
149	
150	## Rules
151	
152	- `core/` is infrastructure only. Features never import features.
153	- Layering is one-way: core -> grammar -> features -> compiler, all
154	  over `@std/relation`, whose `engine/` is the memo kernel —
155	  infrastructure, language-agnostic, the one a running program asks too.
156	  `grammar/` is the language-agnostic engine; `compiler/` is the
157	  driver and the ONE definition of Avra (feature order is branch
158	  order is the language).
159	- No string tags or string-matching to detect behavior.
160	- `_ ->` over our own enums is decided by COUNTING THE ANSWERING
161	  ARMS. One arm answers -> a PROJECTION, and the catch-all is
162	  honest: its contract pins the answer for variants that do not
163	  exist yet. TWO OR MORE answer -> a REGISTRY, and a catch-all there
164	  silently forgets the next variant (`let_name` dropped For's
165	  counter exactly so; `type_decl_name` would have swallowed the next
166	  type-declaring statement). Registries spell every arm — `or`-runs
167	  keep that affordable. Ratcheted as style.registry_catchall AND held by the compiler:
168	  F2040 counts the ANSWERING ARMS over the declared enum and names
169	  the variants a hole would forget. The license is a SPELLING, not a
170	  comment — `rest ->` says the remainder is deliberate, and both the
171	  compiler and the ratchet read it. The two licensed shapes are a
172	  feature matching its own variants (it cannot enumerate other
173	  features') and a loop that DELEGATES the rest to an exhaustive
174	  dispatch — each writes `rest ->` at the site.
175	  AND THE LAW IS ABOUT THE TEST, NOT THE MATCH. For a REGISTRY enum
176	  `is .Variant` IS A CATCH-ALL IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES: a boolean that
177	  asks about ONE variant and falls through for the rest discharges
178	  the registry's obligation no better than `_ ->`, and it is harder
179	  to see. For a PROJECTION enum it stays the right idiom. Two
180	  `RtKind` consumers were written that way (`rt_arg`, `answers_word`
181	  in llvm.av), correct only while the enum had three variants —
182	  widening it to carry C's integer widths would have sent an Avra
183	  `int` into an `i32` seat with no truncation, compiling clean. Both
184	  are exhaustive matches now.
185	  ENFORCEMENT SPLITS FROM THE LAW HERE, deliberately: no grep tells a
186	  registry enum from a projection one, so this gets NO ratchet rule.
187	  The keeper is `make vocab`, a CURATED table naming each registry's
188	  consumers and refusing BOTH shapes inside them — the table says
189	  which registries it holds, and a registry it does not name is
190	  unguarded. Naming the next one IS how this law is enforced.
191	  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES INTO C, where no keeper can follow. The
192	  runtime's `acc_kind_of` was a kind-keyed ternary falling through to
193	  ACC_RECORD — correct for the three kinds that existed when it was
194	  written and wrong from that same day for `KIND_STATIC`, so every
195	  immortal string was filed as a RECORD by `AVRA_MEM_STATS`: the
196	  instrument THIS FILE names as the way to answer a memory question,
197	  miscounting its own data since birth. A C chain keyed on our kinds
198	  carries a registry's obligation and `make vocab` cannot see it, so
199	  spell the kinds there too.
200	  AND THE REASON IT HID GENERALIZES: `RtKind` had three variants from
201	  the day it was written and had not yet grown — it carries six now
202	  — so nothing ever tested the assumption. A KEEPER THAT HAS ONLY
203	  EVER GUARDED A STATIC ENUM IS UNTESTED — the first widening is its
204	  first real test, and that is the worst moment to learn it was only
205	  ever looking for one shape.
206	  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES A PACKAGE BOUNDARY TOO, not only into C.
207	  A registry keyed on ANOTHER PACKAGE'S enum is spelled over NAMES —
208	  `node_value` matches `@std.meta.Node`'s variant names, because a
209	  foreign enum has no typed id here — so no compiler law and no grep
210	  sees it, and its `_ -> null` forgot the next variant the way every
211	  registry hole does: a template generated nothing and nobody was
212	  told. The keeper cannot follow across the seam; spell the arms and
213	  make the unknown SPEAK.
214	- THE EXEMPTION LAW, which the above is one instance of: a doctrine
215	  exemption that is not written AT THE SITE is an unbounded amnesty.
216	  Prose exemptions are invisible to tooling and to the next reader,
217	  so they rot into the default. Every licensed deviation carries
218	  `// LICENSED I<n>: <reason>` where the code is — that is what
219	  makes `make idioms` able to demand a decision instead of guessing
220	  which deviations were once approved.
221	- Node facts (spans included) live in side tables keyed by typed ids,
222	  never on nodes.
223	- A SLOT'S SEED IS COMPUTED THE SAME WAY AS ITS UPDATES, or the
224	  first decision judges a different quantity from every later one —
225	  and only the first, which is what makes it invisible.
226	  `collapse_breaks` seeded `line_indent` from `raw[0].span.lo`, a
227	  byte OFFSET, and assigned it a character DISTANCE everywhere after;
228	  the seed read as a column only while the first token sat on line
229	  one, so a LEADING COMMENT's own length became the indent and a
230	  four-character comment changed how the file parsed. Write the seed
231	  as the update's rule applied to nothing, not as whatever value
232	  happens to be at hand.
233	- A fact EVERY BODY MAY READ is answered from the PROGRAM — the
234	  store — never from a pass's fact tables. Fact tables are per
235	  declaration, over that declaration's expression range alone, so an
236	  answer computed from `facts` is right in the body that recorded it
237	  and WRONG everywhere else (a const's declared `int?` read back as
238	  `int` across a fn floor, and `??` warned it would never fire).
239	  The store holds what the program wrote; that is what shared
240	  answers are made of.
241	- A law that HOLDS A BINDING TO ITS ANNOTATION compares the value to
242	  the DECLARED type it computed, never to the binding's own type —
243	  asking the binding for its type compares the value against itself,
244	  and the law silently stops refusing anything.
245	- Ask a BINDING, never a NAME, whether it is a const/a capture/a
246	  seat. A name may be defined twice (a `let` shadowing a const), so
247	  a name-keyed question and the binding in hand answer about
248	  DIFFERENT statements — the mismatch reads a slot nobody wrote
249	  ("index -1"). One question, asked of the statement. And a
250	  name-keyed table holds what it holds: `resolve_assign` asked
251	  `binding_of(name)`, a LOCALS table, so a fn's name walked
252	  through as a place — the walk had already recorded the root's
253	  binding; ask that.
254	- A BODY IS TYPED UNDER ITS SIGNATURE, so a declaration whose
255	  SIGNATURE WAS REFUSED has no scope for its body to be typed in —
256	  and the empty list that stands in for the missing one is read as
257	  a real scope by every seat. `walk_under` sets `self.scope =
258	  sig?.params ?? []`, the plausible default the protocol law
259	  refuses, and `target_type`'s `.Param(i) -> self.scope[i]` then
260	  indexed past the end: a generic METHOD is refused whole (F2031,
261	  no sig recorded) and its body still walks, so `fn f<T: Tr>(x: T)
262	  { x.m() }` inside an `impl` CRASHED THE COMPILER while the same
263	  fn at the top level was fine. The tell was a SIBLING PAIR
264	  disagreeing in one match — `.Receiver -> self.scope.first() ??
265	  self.error_type` was total and `.Param(i)` was not, four lines
266	  apart, so one seat kind had the guard and the other did not.
267	  SEVERAL SPELLINGS OF ONE QUESTION IS THE DEFECT, not the missing
268	  bound: every one asks "what type does seat i wear", and one file
269	  held five — two receiver reads, total, and three parameter reads,
270	  none of them. The split was invisible because each pair sat
271	  inside ONE match, arms apart, so a reader checking either arm saw
272	  a guard right beside it. There is one reader now (`seat_type`),
273	  and the refusal was already spoken before the body ran, which is
274	  what makes Error the honest answer rather than a defect voice.
275	- A COPIED TEMPLATE'S SPANS ARE ITS ORIGIN FILE'S OFFSETS — so its
276	  errors point home — and any pass that reads a span as THIS file's
277	  offset must ask `store.spanned_elsewhere(e)` first. `range_bodies`
278	  did not, and `within`'s copied nodes landed in whatever `client.av`
279	  declared at `time.av`'s offsets (a write through `self` blamed on
280	  `describe`). A sublanguage's nodes are foreign too but spanned HERE
281	  (shifted into the block); `ForeignRange.spanned_home` tells them apart.
282	- A READ WEARS THE TYPE OF WHAT IS READ, never the type of the node
283	  doing the reading. This bit THREE times in one slice: a captured
284	  callee took the CALL's type (a call's type is its answer, never its
285	  callee's), a capture took the LAMBDA's type (a lambda is a managed
286	  box, so an `int` capture looked managed and the memory pass
287	  retained a number), and a field read took the field expression's
288	  type where the SUBJECT's decides the layout. A register's recorded
289	  type is the wrong witness under mono, where it may still name a
290	  type parameter; the STATIC type of the thing being read is right.
291	- UNIFY BINDS, `accepts` RECORDS. `unify` agrees two types and pins a
292	  declaration's Vars; it does NOT record the lift that lowering
293	  mints. A seat that unifies and returns without passing through the
294	  agreement door silently drops the widen — invisible for as long as
295	  the widen happens to be identity, and a wrong answer the day the
296	  representation changes. The door is ONE verb, `agreed` (checks.av),
297	  and the three unified seats — a call argument, a struct field, an
298	  enum payload — call it; the payload once short-circuited and
299	  refused a `dyn` box and an auto-Ok its siblings took
300	  (compiler/tests/seats holds the proof).
301	- EVERY POINTER AVRA HOLDS CARRIES A HEADER. The runtime counts
302	  references in sixteen bytes BEFORE each payload (tag, kind, rc,
303	  and a LENGTH — a string's text length, a record's payload bytes),
304	  and `avra_rc_retain/release` read that header — so a managed
305	  value that came from anywhere else reads memory that is not ours.
306	  The sources are all headered: the backend's string constants
307	  (`avra_llvm_build_text`, kind STATIC, immortal),
308	  the runtime's own words (`avra_bool_text`, "null"), argv and the
309	  environment (`str_static`). A new C fn that answers TEXT to a
310	  program allocates it with `box_alloc`/`str_owned`, or
311	  `str_static` when the program must never own it — never a bare
312	  `malloc` or a C literal. The tag is the belt (`hdr` refuses a
313	  header without it, and an unaligned or null-page address before
314	  reading anything); the law is the braces. THE FLOOR IS THE NULL
315	  PAGE, NEVER THE IMAGE BASE: a 4 GB floor held only while the loader
316	  put everything high, so under valgrind (and any non-PIE image)
317	  every box read as foreign — nothing counted, nothing freed, every
318	  constant copied — and the first Linux profile reported that as the
319	  program.
320	- A CELL WEARS ITS BINDING'S DECLARED TYPE, never its first value's,
321	  and A STORE SETTLES BY THE CELL'S TYPE, never the value's. `mut x:
322	  T? = null` seeded a cell in the null's own type (the widen from
323	  null into a boxed nullable is identity, so no register ever wore
324	  `T?`), the memory pass saw no managed cell to settle, and whatever
325	  the cell held at the scope's end leaked — every `farthest` fold in
326	  the executor kept its last far record, 600 MB of a self-check —
327	  while `x = null` released nothing. The runtime's accounting found
328	  both; a flat struct's nullable hid them (that widen mints a box).
329	- A CLOSURE STORED IN A VALUE THAT CAPTURES THE VALUE'S OWNER IS A
330	  CYCLE, and counting never frees a cycle. The workspace's query
331	  verifiers, its declaration table's hooks and every Analysis in its
332	  table capture the workspace: no workspace could die, and 1674 spec
333	  cases kept 1674 of them — 922 MB in the test binary. A ONE-SHOT
334	  workspace ends its own cycles (`disarmed`, at `Language.analyze`)
335	  once the analysis it was made for has run: nothing re-verifies at
336	  revision one, every sig it will ask for is held, and an Analysis
337	  asked after is remade over the memoized parts, never kept. The
338	  language's answer is in the sugar backlog: weak captures.
339	- ONE DERIVATION IS ALIVE AT A TIME. A derivation that turns, owes
340	  its instantiations, or quarrels under a hold is asked AGAIN in a
341	  fresh workspace, and the one before must be LET GO first or the
342	  build's peak is their SUM — a file test then its directory's passed
343	  5 GB where either alone is 2.2. Three holders keep one alive, and
344	  each needs its own answer. THE STACK: a caller's binding stands for
345	  the whole call, so the derivation that is superseded is bound in a
346	  HELPER that returns the next attempt and dies (`stood_first`,
347	  `heard`, `tried_anew`), never in the fn that asks again. THE HOOKS:
348	  `Workspace.discarded()` ends every one, the registry's declare hook
349	  among them — it captures the table that holds the registry, and
350	  EVERY HOOK A `Decls` ARMS is cleared in `let_go`: the four producer
351	  doors were not, and each turned attempt stood beside the next
352	  (419 MB against 77); `make hooks-released` diffs the hook fields
353	  against `disarm`/`let_go` and names the one left armed. THE
354	  PROCESS: a relation's rows stand in a process-wide store under their
355	  Db until `close()`, whoever else died. `make turn-memory-attack`
356	  holds it by memory: a rebuild that turns twelve times, under a
357	  ceiling one attempt clears and their sum trips.
358	- A VALUE ITS OWN HOOKS CAPTURE IS AN IDENTITY, AND A COPY FORKS IT.
359	  `mut q = p` is a copy (spec 11.5), hooks included: the copy's writes
360	  land in the copy while its hooks answer for the original. The
361	  workspace is one (its families and its table's hooks capture it), so
362	  `check`'s `mut ws = o.ws` — a workspace read out of a record — lost
363	  every std package admitted after the copy, and a compiler built by a
364	  compiler that copies read `@std.meta`'s own `Kind` as undefined (522
365	  errors). MINT AN IDENTITY IN THE BINDING THAT WRITES IT (`mut ws =
366	  build_workspace(path)`), and read F2106 as naming exactly this.
367	  features/tests/borrow_identity is the one-generation witness. AND
368	  THE SWEEP THAT ACQUITTED THE TREE READ ONE PACKAGE: five lanes paid
369	  "the 15 sites" of `check packages/std-avrac`, and the two that broke
370	  were in `packages/cli`, warned about the whole time.
371	- A READ-MODIFY-WRITE THROUGH `get` IS A COPY, AND THE COPY IS WHOLE.
372	  `mut t = c.get()`, a write through `t`, `c.set(t)` is correct under
373	  spec 11.5 and COPIES what the cell holds on every turn — `get`
374	  answers a copy (the owner's Q2(a)), and F2106 names the local. When
375	  the loop is hot the copy is quadratic: the memo's settle did it per
376	  query until `Table` became ONE SHARED SLOT (a `Cell` of rows, an
377	  in-place `keep`). Write in place through the holder's own verbs —
378	  `put`, `push`, `set_at` on the cell, or a type that owns its cell —
379	  and keep `get`-then-`set` for values nobody writes often.
380	- A PARAMETER IS BORROWED, AND WHAT A CALLEE KEEPS TAKES ITS OWN
381	  REFERENCE. The caller keeps every managed argument STANDING for
382	  the call — a param, a register a scope owns, a cell's load and the
383	  binary's own data stand already; a VIEW into a box does not, since
384	  the callee may empty that box, so it is held across the call
385	  (memory.av's `standing_regs`, `lent`). The callee owns none of its
386	  params: a store, a push, a pack, a yield and its ANSWER each take
387	  a reference of their own, as any value a scope does not own does.
388	  A call that only reads costs no count at all — callee-cleans spent
389	  a retain and a release a managed seat, 1.3 billion counts in one
390	  cold `check` of the cli and 15% of its CPU. THE PROOF IS
391	  features/fns/tests/borrowed_params, each rule witnessed failing
392	  without it under `AVRA_RC_GUARD=1`. AND THE TYPE STILL DECIDES: a
393	  seat typed as unmanaged (`Ptr`, `Int`) is a view never held and an
394	  answer never retained — a read of freed memory. The capture lane
395	  read as `Ptr` was one (`callee_binding`), and a mut fn CELL loaded
396	  at the call's answer type was its twin (the box read as `i64`, LLVM
397	  refused). The fourth and fifth instances of A READ WEARS THE
398	  TYPE OF WHAT IS READ: a capture wears the CAPTURED binding's
399	  type, seated by typing (`TypeFacts.captures`), a cell's load the
400	  DEFINITION's (`def_type_of`) — at every read that MINTS, which
401	  in `callee_binding` is exactly those two.
402	- A FN TYPE CARRIES ITS SEATS' CONTRACT: `fn(mut Cx, int) -> int`
403	  is a DIFFERENT TYPE from `fn(Cx, int) -> int`, and the interner
404	  keeps them apart (the marks ride the key). That is the missing
405	  half of the seat law: without it a `mut`-taking fn stored in a
406	  plain fn seat wrote through an immutable `let` with no diagnostic,
407	  in both engines. The law has ONE asymmetry, and it is the sound
408	  direction — a seat that PERMITS writing accepts a callee that does
409	  not write (`fn_fits`), a seat that promised not to write refuses
410	  one that does. A fn type's marks are NORMALIZED at `intern` (the
411	  trailing unwritten ones dropped), so `fn(T)` built with no marks
412	  and with two false ones are one type; skip that and two spellings
413	  of one type refuse each other with identical words on both sides.
414	  The seat law then reads MARKS, never a DeclId, so a declared
415	  callee and a fn-typed value are one rule: `declared_marks`
416	  projects a declaration into the same currency.
417	  AND A SEAT'S PROMISES ARE ONE CHANNEL: `SeatMark { mutable,
418	  settled }`, carried as a `List<SeatMark>` on `Type.Fn`, `Arrow`,
419	  `TypeRef` and `Param` — never a parallel `List<bool>` per promise.
420	  A promise added as a second list doubles every mark site and drops
421	  silently wherever a site forgets it (the `TypeRef` default-field
422	  bug, twice); added as a FIELD it reaches every reader through the
423	  one `mark_at`, and `intern` normalizes one shape. The spelling
424	  boundary is the one exception: `TypeLit.Fn` keeps the grammar's
425	  two written lists and `interned` zips them once, so the currency
426	  never leaks into a user's `interned` receiver.
427	- A TYPE MIGRATION CAN MOVE WHO HOLDS A VALUE, AND A LIFETIME PROMISE
428	  IS A PROMISE ABOUT THE HOLDER. Changing a seat's type is arithmetic
429	  on signatures until the value's PROVENANCE changes — then a
430	  caller-held box silently becomes a CALLEE-MINTED one. @std/sqlite's
431	  `bind_text_unsafely_borrowed(…, value: string)` promises the
432	  caller's bytes outlive the statement, and is keepable only because
433	  the caller's own box goes straight through; migrating the WALL seat
434	  to `Bytes` while the FACE kept `string` would force the face to
435	  call `.bytes()` — minting a box whose only holder is that call,
436	  dead at return, handing C a dangling pointer every time with the
437	  caller having done nothing wrong. The face takes the new type too,
438	  so the box stays in the caller's hands and the type says what the
439	  contract always required. THE SEATS WHERE THIS BITES ARE FEW AND
440	  GREPPABLE: those whose contract mentions LIFETIME.
441	  One level down, the same law: a box materialised ONLY to be staged
442	  has no other holder, so its last reference dies before the call and
443	  C reads freed memory — staged boxes are held until the call
444	  returns, and the engines disagreeing is how it was seen.
445	  (Attributed to the sqlite lead and the substrate lane: `Bytes` is
446	  not on main. The seat, its contract and its `string` type ARE here,
447	  so the hazard is live for whoever migrates it.)
448	- A SETTLED AGGREGATE IS STATIC DATA, AND ITS BUFFER IS THE
449	  BINARY'S. A const's list, record, enum or map is laid out as an
450	  immortal headered global (`Ins.StaticAddr`, features/statics.av;
451	  the runtime's layouts are ONE definition, runtime/avra_box.h, that
452	  the backend mirrors and static-asserts). A read is an address; the
453	  memory pass owes it nothing. The runtime never frees or reallocs
454	  what it did not allocate: `array_grow` moves a laid-out buffer's
455	  cells out (`laid_out`), and a static map's index is BUILT ON FIRST
456	  LOOKUP, sized for its keys — one hash, the runtime's, never a copy
457	  in the compiler. AND A FIX THAT IS THE LAW CAN STILL TRAP THE
458	  COMPILER: opening every `mut`-seat argument unique (a copy is a
459	  copy) trapped the product's own `check` with "index 304 is out of
460	  bounds" — the compiler's source rides that write-through channel
461	  (ROADMAP H3b) — and the way it was told apart from a broken tree
462	  was the pre-fix product checking the SAME source clean. When a
463	  second-generation product traps, run the first generation over the
464	  same source before reading the trap as the tree's.
465	- THE `avra` SHIM MOVES TO THE TREE'S ROOT, so "." inside a command is
466	  the TREE and `PWD` follows the move: `docs <name>` and `process`
467	  (then spelled `explain @name` and `explain process`) rooted at "."
468	  analysed nothing from the day they landed,
469	  and read as "no fn declared in this package" for a fn declared
470	  right there. The caller's directory is `AVRA_CWD`, exported by the
471	  shim before it moves; a command that reads the package it stands in
472	  roots at `here()` (cli/commands/shared.av), never at ".", and EVERY
473	  PATH ARGUMENT is rooted there too, ABSOLUTELY (`rooted`) — a
474	  relative one read where the tree stands found nothing from another
475	  directory, and read from a package's own root it walked past the
476	  `avra.toml` at `.`; one absolute spelling serves both. AND THE
477	  SHIM'S HEAVINESS TEST SKIPS THE SUBCOMMAND WORD: `build/` is a
478	  directory at the tree's root, so every `avra build <file>` queued
479	  on the machine lock as a package-scale run until the loop learned
480	  to start at the second word. AND A
481	  PACKAGE IS NAMED BY ONE VERB: a root module carries no package
482	  prefix, so `package_of_module` answered "" for the root while the
483	  manifest named it — `Decls.package_named` answers the root's
484	  manifest name (dotted) for both the declaration read and the file
485	  view's, and the orphan-impl law, which compares the two, refused
486	  every impl in the compiler's own cli the moment only one side knew.
487	  A second-generation build that REFUSES its own source is this law's
488	  symptom as much as a trap is.
489	- A POINTER SEAT NAMES ITS BOX. A row's `Ptr` says a header stands
490	  there, not WHICH — and `avra_str_len` handed a list answers the
491	  list's byte size as a text length, in a clean program (native 40,
492	  the evaluator "defect"). `RtSig.boxes` (core/ir.av's `Box`: `Text`,
493	  `List`, `Map`, `Any`) says what each pointer seat reads; a row that
494	  names none takes `Any` everywhere — unconstrained, never wrongly
495	  constrained, since most pointer seats do take any box and
496	  `avra_rc_retain` means it. TWO READERS, ONE COLUMN: `checked_extern`
497	  refuses an `extern fn` that names a row with the wrong seat count
498	  or a type that is not the seat's box (F2084; `ptr` is the raw
499	  crossing and fits any), and `make externs` refuses a `Text` box over
500	  a C `void*` or a `char*` under any other — so the column, the C and
501	  every declaration agree or the gate says which does not. Filled from
502	  the C in one sweep (46 rows, 141 seats): `const char*` is `Text`;
503	  the array, map and process rows say `List`/`Map` by name.
504	- AN `extern fn` WITH A BODY DEFINES ITS SYMBOL; ONE WITHOUT NAMES
505	  ONE. `extern fn avra_ui_event(who: int, …) { … }` is a HOST FN: the
506	  host calls it by exactly that name, a non-host target exports it from
507	  WHEREVER IT IS DECLARED, and a bodiless `extern fn` of the name in
508	  any file is answered by it — which is how a test answers a host's
509	  row in Avra (std-ui's `web/tests/mount` answers `avra_dom_frame`, so
510	  the one module that names the page runs eval == native). `export` is
511	  a module's visibility and exports nothing to a host. Its seats and
512	  answer are plain `int`, `float`, `string`, `Bytes` or `ptr`
513	  (type.host_fn); two of one name in a program are refused
514	  (lower.host_fn_twice). The backend defines the bare symbol beside the
515	  body under the extern row's shape; the evaluator, which has no
516	  linker, turns a call of the name into a call of the body
517	  (`hosted_within`).
518	  AND A SYMBOL IS THE WHOLE LINK'S, so three things are held where the
519	  host fn stands (compiler/whole.av's `host_fn_owes`). WHO OPENS IT: a
520	  dependency's host fn is the program's export only when the program's
521	  OWN sources import that package (lower.host_fn_unasked), and a build
522	  lists each as `host fn: <package> <name>`, fresh or kept. AND A
523	  DEPENDENCY'S HOST FN NAMES ITS HOST: `@host(Host.Page)` (`@std/meta`,

1611	  (`cx.scope_enter()`/`cx.scope_exit(r)`) or a statement-list arm
1612	  (`cx.arm_stmts(stmts)`) — never a raw `Ins.ScopeEnter`/`ScopeExit`
1613	  through a LowerCx, never a bare `cx.lower_stmts` inside an arm. A
1614	  raw bracket is invisible to the frames, so a `defer` inside it
1615	  runs at the ENCLOSING frame's end (an `if` statement's branch did
1616	  exactly that). The seats' bracket in lower_fn/lower_lambda is
1617	  `seats_enter/seats_exit` — no statement list, no frame — so a
1618	  body's block is depth 1 and its close is the fn's TAIL. And an
1619	  early exit calls `cx.leaving(answer)` (an answer — an `errdefer`
1620	  runs behind its tag when it is a failing `Result`) or
1621	  `cx.failing()` (the failure channel — `fail`, `?` — which runs
1622	  `errdefer`s unconditionally) BEFORE its `Ins.FnExit`: the value is
1623	  computed, the deferred calls come next, then the exit.

1627	What our compiler REFUSES that the language will want. THE SECTION IS
1628	EXECUTABLE: every refusal below is a case in
1629	`packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests/subset/` pinning its kind, its
1630	words and its message count, and every fact under "Runtime facts" is a

1632	turns its case red — delete the case and its line together. A new entry
1633	lands WITH its case; a line without one says so. Each entry is a
1634	sugar-backlog candidate, not a trap to write around: write the form the
1635	compiler's help names, and when a site wants the missing form, add the
1636	ask to the ROADMAP's sugar backlog naming the site. Laws that SPEAK are
1637	not listed — reserved words (F3002), a mutating method on a non-`mut`
1638	binding (F2034), a lambda assigning to a capture (F3005), a fn body
1639	reading a top-level `let` (F3020), an extra method inside an `impl
1640	Trait for` (F2032), an exported name declared twice across a module's

1644	Syntax the grammar lacks:
1645	- An import is spelled with DOTS: `use @std.io.{read_text}`; `use @std/io.{…}` is "expected `.`" at the slash (prose says `@std/io`, the `use` line never does).
1646	- Or-patterns spell `or`, in patterns only; `|` is "expected `}` to close the `match`", and `or`/`and` as booleans are "expected BREAK" — the operators are `&&`, `||`, `!`.
1647	- `[i for (i, m) in xs.enumerate()]` — "`enumerate` pairs only under a paired `for` head"; write `[f(i, x) for i, x in xs]`.
1648	- `int??` has no spelling ("expected `)`"/"expected `=`" at the first `?`) though a generic reaches `string??`.
1649	- A bare `table { … }` reads as a struct literal ("no `type table` is declared"); write `table<Row> { id | name … }` with a pipe header.
1650	- A record literal as a component instance's head stands in parentheses (`tally (Span { n: 2 }) { extra: 3 }`); bare, the brace opens the block — pinned by features/components/tests/components_head_test.av, not by this section.
1651	- A semicolon between statements is "unexpected character `;`"; a one-line body is `{ a }`.
1652	- A field's mark on its own line inside a type literal is "expected `}` while parsing `stmt`"; write it on the field's line (`{ @local at: int }`).
1653	- `if let v? = e { … }` takes an `else`: without one it is "expected BREAK" at the `let`; a guard is `let v? = e else { … }`, and a present-only test is `if e != null { … }`.
1654	- A range takes methods (`any`, `find`, `map`, `all`) but has no `.length`.
1655	- A `once fn` takes no type parameters ("expected `(`"), no arguments, and answers a managed value ("`once fn seed` answers `int`, which the runtime cannot keep").
1656	- A trailing block in a head (`if f(a) { x -> x } { … }`) is "expected BREAK"; parenthesise the call. `a?.m { … }` and `(f(a)) { … }` take no trailing block either — not pinned.
1657	- A seat default lands on `fn`, `mut fn`, `static fn` and a trait's `fn` (whose default every impl takes) only: `extern fn` and a lambda refuse it ("expected `)`", "expected `)` to close the group"); a named argument skips a defaulted seat; a default reads no sibling param; a fn value of a defaulted fn wears every seat.
1658	- A generic fn as a value: pinned `ident<int>` is "expected BREAK"; bare is "a generic fn is not a value — no single signature to wear".
1659	- Instantiation is a statement: as a fn's tail it answers `void` — bind, then return the name; a component block is `key: value` ("declares no `List` field, so its block holds settings only") — not pinned.
1660	- A shell `${VAR}` in a string is Avra's interpolation ("`HOME` is not defined", or silently the binding's value); write `$VAR`.
1661	- `_` is a parameter name nowhere ("`_` is a keyword"); an unread seat is `_q`, and `let _ = f()` is the binding spelling.
1662	- A map's keys are strings only ("a map's keys are strings, not `int`").
1663	- `xs ++ ys` is "expected BREAK"; `xs.concat(ys)` or `[..xs, ..ys]`.
1664	- `List` has `all`, not `every`.
1665	- A spread's refusals are laws, not pending sugar (`..` is one spelling in a record literal, list, map, variadic seat, call's named seats and pattern): a record spreads only under its type's name (`{ ..a, x: 3 }` is a map: "`..` in a map spreads a map, found `P`"); a record pattern's `..` discards, so `P { x, ..rest }` is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; a list spreads only into its own element type; `f(..xs)` into fixed seats is "`..` spreads into a seat that takes the rest of the arguments"; `is` over a list or record pattern binds only under `if` (`type.is_bind`) and a refutable destructuring `let` needs its `else` (`type.let_pattern`).
1666	- A match arm on the brace's line needs a trailing comma before the next arm ("expected `}` to close the `match`", reported at the second arm); each arm on its own line parses.
1667	- A present-bind arm (`v? -> …`) after a comma-ended arm, or itself ending in a comma, is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; separate such arms by line.
1668	- An empty block as a match arm is an empty map: "a `match`'s arms disagree: `{}` vs the first arm's `void`".
1669	- A `\u` escape is not one: `"\u0041"` keeps its six characters, as do `\0` and `\u{…}` (see Runtime facts); spell a code point with `@std/text`'s `from_codepoint(65533)` and a NUL with `from_codepoint(0)` (sugar backlog: `\u{…}` escapes).
1670	- A bare name in a pattern is a const's or a binder's by its binding, never its spelling: `type.const_pattern` warns when a match ENDS on a const's name and `type.unreachable_arm` when a binder precedes a literal arm (the const-comparison law itself is not pinned here; features/enums/tests/const_pat_template is).
1671	- A match arm whose body is a bare statement (`.Bad(t) -> fail E.Bad(t),`) fails the whole file ("expected `}` to close the `match`"); brace it.
1672	- `get(i)?.name` and `shell(line)?.run()` lex as `?.` ("`?.` reaches into a nullable, this is `Result<…>`"); write `(get(i)?).name`.
1673	- `export let` is "`export` marks a fn, type, enum or trait — not this statement"; `export const` lands.
1674	- `Result<void, E>` is "a `Result` side cannot hold `void` yet"; a writing verb answers what it wrote.
1675	- A `mut` seat cannot be assigned whole, by design: "a seat is written along a path, never replaced whole" — use a `Cell<T>`, a path write, or answer the new value.
1676	- Two top-level consts of one name are "defined more than once"; a `let` of that name shadows from its line on, and a fn body reads the const.
1677	- `fail` inside a `catch` arm's block is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side"; write the statement `match`.
1678	- `[null, null]` names no type where no seat names one ("a list element takes its type from its value"); any typed sibling or seat names it.
1679	- A keyed list (`list xs by it.id { x -> … }`) is "`list` takes no head value"; reconciliation is positional — not pinned (needs `@std/ui`).
1680	- `derived x = …` and `query x = …` are "expected BREAK"; recompute in a `fn` or hold a `state`.
1681	- `@model type` is "`model` is not defined"; a plain `type` until the derive exists.
1682	- A built-in type name is no domain type: `type Task = { … }` is "`Task` is a built-in type".
1683	
1684	Wants the typer does not carry yet:
1685	- A declaring annotation's argument is a literal or a const naming one: `@traced("a" + "b")` is "`traced` generates declarations, so its arguments come from the source alone" — not pinned (needs a package with `@std/meta`).
1686	- A generic struct literal's field seat unifies instead of planting a want: an unpinned `mk()` there is "`N` is not pinned by the arguments".
1687	- A lambda in a field or argument seat does not read the seat's answer ("`.Ok` needs a known enum"); a typed `let` does, and a named fn works everywhere.
1688	- `Traced<E>`'s `cause`/`context`/`trace` stay inherent methods permanently (a trait member's answer is fixed by its signature); the real want is a bound on a type's own parameter.
1689	- A bound lands on a free fn's and a component's parameters only: `type T<K: Tr, V>` and `impl T<K: Tr, V>` are "expected `=`"/"expected `{`", a generic method is "generic methods are recorded, not landed"; a generic container keyed by a typed id keys by the slot (core's `SideTable`).
1690	- Variant arms or `is` over a nullable enum are "`match` chooses over an enum, found `K?`" / "`is` asks an enum for its variant, found `K?`"; unwrap first.
1691	- A bound method as a value (`xs.any(self.rides)`) is read as a property ("no field `rides` on `S`"); write `(k) -> self.rides(k)`.
1692	- `it` through a self-method wrapper (`xs.any(self.rides(it))`) is "`it` has no element here"; `it` binds to the nearest call, and a pipe stage is such a call.
1693	- `[1, 2].join(",")` is "`join` reads a list of text, this one holds `int`"; map to text first.
1694	- `==`, `contains`/`index_of` and a literal pattern compare a scalar, text, a tagged enum, or a one-field record; two fields is "`==` compares by value — …", and an enum carrying a payload is refused too (help: match on it).
1695	- A named type is opaque at a seat and transparent at a read: a `Rows` seat refuses a computed `List<int>` ("wants `Rows`, found `List<int>`") and takes a literal.
1696	- `r catch null` answers the ok side, so `let x? = r catch null else { … }` is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side: `D`, this is `null`" (and "`x?` asks a nullable"); a `Result` read as absence is a `match` (`.Ok(d) -> d, .Err(_) -> null`).

1698	Methods the runtime lacks:
1699	- `List.reverse()` / `sort()` are "calls a method, and `List<int>` has none"; core's `reversed` is the helper.
1700	- `m["k"]` on a map is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Map<string, int>`"; `.get(k)` answers `T?`.
1701	- `b[0]` on `Bytes` is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Bytes`"; `b.at(i)` reads an octet and traps past the end. `[104, 105].bytes()` answers `Bytes?` ("declares `Bytes`, this is `Bytes?`"), and `.at` on it is refused.

1704	- `split` drops a trailing empty segment and keeps a leading one (`".a"` two, `"a."` one, `""` none).
1705	- `"\u0041".length` is 6, `"ab\0cd".length` is 6 and `"\u{1F600}".length` is 9 — no `\u` or `\0` is an escape.

1709	## How work lands
1710	
1711	The single source for the landing path, Sprites, the watcher and the
1712	CI gates is `docs/2026_10_11_THE_PIPELINE.md`; the section below is the
1713	doctrine it expands.
1714	
1715	- ALL WORK MOVES THROUGH SEVEN COMMANDS, and nothing else touches main:
1716	
1717	      sh tools/work new <name>   # a worktree ../avra-<name> off main, and its Sprite
1718	      sh tools/work run <cmd>    # run it on a GitHub runner (--sprite: the lane's Sprite), its exit status
1719	      sh tools/work test         # what this branch touches, on this lane's Sprite
1720	      sh tools/work land         # push, PR, arm auto-merge — no Sprite involved
1721	      sh tools/work status       # PRs and their merge state; each lane and its Sprite
1722	      sh tools/work sprites      # every Sprite at a glance; `--fix [name]` repairs
1723	      sh tools/work unbind       # end this lane's run, free its Sprite, keep the worktree
1724	      sh tools/work done --remove-worktree   # remove this lane too: ONLY with the owner's say-so
1725	
1726	  Main lives on GitHub (avra-lang/avra): squash merges, linear history,
1727	  no direct pushes. It requires the `test` check AND that a branch be up
1728	  to date with it, and auto-merge lands a green, current PR by itself,
1729	  one at a time. A local main
1730	  only follows `origin/main` (the reference-transaction hook refuses any
1731	  other update; a deliberate repair sets `AVRA_MAIN_OVERRIDE="<reason>"`).
1732	- THE PR IS THE TRAIN, AND THERE IS NO MERGE QUEUE (dropped 2026-10-11:
1733	  its only real value was testing `main` plus every PR ahead, which
1734	  "require up to date" gives back for free one PR at a time, while the
1735	  queue cost trains that tested many PRs at once — one red suite killed
1736	  them all — HEADGREEN batching and a rebase treadmill). A PR's `test`
1737	  check IS the gate, on the PR's own tree (`.github/workflows/
1738	  checks.yml`): fmt on its changed `.av`, idioms and suites over the
1739	  packages it TOUCHES, the compiler-dependent keepers, the seed check and
1740	  the affected packages' suites; a PR that touches no `.av`, no package
1741	  and no compiler source builds nothing. Before it builds anything it
1742	  runs the keepers that need NO COMPILER (`make keepers-static`, half a
1743	  minute), so a refusal one of them speaks stops on the PR. Because the
1744	  branch must be up to date, the tree it tests already holds `main`, so a
1745	  cross-PR interaction (two individually-green PRs
1746	  colliding on a latent bug) is caught on the later PR's own run. THE
1747	  COMPILER IS CACHED BY
1748	  ITS OWN SOURCE (`tools/compiler_paths.sh`): a tree whose compiler is
1749	  main's takes main's binary; otherwise the newest cached binary builds
1750	  the tree twice (the generation law), and one too old to read it — new
1751	  syntax, a new refusal about its own source — fails that build and the
1752	  tree BOOTSTRAPS from the committed seed. Main's own push run caches
1753	  the compiler every run starts from.
1754	- A LANE ITERATES WITH `make try`, NEVER `make avra`: it builds the
1755	  compiler with the STANDING `build/avra` into `build/avra-try` and never
1756	  replaces the builder, so its store stays warm (a leaf edit, ~4 s held
1757	  464/466) and `./avra-try <cmd>` probes the change. `make avra` is for
1758	  a change the compiler must READ to build itself — codegen, the front
1759	  end, a refusal about its own source — and before landing.
1760	- A PRE-COMMIT HOOK refuses staged `.av` that is not canonical; the fix
1761	  it prints is `build/avra fmt --write <files>`. Never `--no-verify`.
1762	- HEAVY RUNS GO ON SPRITES, ONE SPRITE A LANE: `sh tools/work run <cmd>`
1763	  from inside the worktree. `work new` binds a free Sprite (`work bind`
1764	  for a worktree that has none, `work unbind` frees it), and the lane's
1765	  tree and compiler stay warm there between runs. Bootstraps, whole
1766	  suites and censuses run there; the Mac keeps quick targeted checks and
1767	  anything macOS-only. ONE RUN PER SPRITE, EVERY STEP BOUNDED: `run`
1768	  answers the command's status, or 76 (busy), 70 (the compiler does not
1769	  build), 124/125 (a bound; `--for <minutes>` raises the command's), 137
1770	  (out of memory), 75 (the Sprite did not answer), 74 (the provider did
1771	  not answer) — and a failure's last line begins with the one of three
1772	  that failed: SPRITE, CONNECTION or COMMAND. A RUN BELONGS TO THE
1773	  SPRITE, NOT TO THE CONNECTION: a supervisor there keeps its output and
1774	  status and holds the Sprite awake while it lives, `run` only follows
1775	  it, and a dropped connection is followed again from the byte it stood
1776	  at — so Ctrl-C or `work stop` ends a run; a drop, a hangup or the
1777	  client being killed never does (it says so, and the next `run` answers
1778	  76 until `work attach` has followed it out); a run is as long as its
1779	  `--for` says, and the Sprite ends it at its bound whoever is
1780	  watching (`work attach` follows again, `work stop` ends it, `work
1781	  done` ends it with the lane). `sh tools/work sprites` shows all of
1782	  them in seconds.
1783	  A RUN ANSWERS ABOUT THIS WORKTREE OR NOT AT ALL: rsync carries files
1784	  to the Sprite, a file the worktree no longer has is removed there by
1785	  name, and the Sprite's manifest (every path and its hash) must equal
1786	  the worktree's before anything starts — else `SPRITE — sync:` and 75.
1787	  What a run wrote is left: `build/`, `.avra-cache`, anything git ignores.
1788	  WHAT ENDS A RUN EARLY IS MEMORY, NOT TIME: a twenty-minute exec holds,
1789	  chatty or silent, and thirty-two spinning processes leave a Sprite
1790	  answering in a second — but a Sprite says 16 GB and a balloon holds
1791	  half, more while it idles (3.3 to 7.3 GB were free to a run), there is
1792	  no swap, and under about 250 MB the whole machine answers nobody for
1793	  minutes. The Sprite's keeper ends a run at 600 MB (137), and every run
1794	  says what it had to start with. A SPRITE WITH NO SESSION AND NO HOLD
1795	  IS SUSPENDED WITHIN SECONDS, MID-WRITE IF NEED BE, which is why
1796	  nothing runs there detached without the hold; one silent for minutes
1797	  has lost its filesystem and is destroyed and created again
1798	  (provisioning is `run`'s first step, from `.github/ci/packages.txt`).
1799	  WHAT HOLDS A SPRITE AWAKE WITH NOBODY ATTACHED IS ITS TASKS API AND
1800	  NOTHING ELSE WE TRIED, measured over 400 s without contact: a task
1801	  refreshed each minute, no gap; a detached TTY session that prints, no
1802	  gap; a running service, a 372 s gap; outbound traffic, frozen at once;
1803	  an exec from outside every 20 s, one tick each. And a task's name is
1804	  lowercase letters, digits and dashes or the Sprite answers 400 — a
1805	  run is named after the machine that began it, capitals and all, so the
1806	  hold is asked under a name made to fit and ITS ANSWER IS READ. A run
1807	  that stood still says for how long in its own output, and `work
1808	  sprites` shows it beside how long the run has been quiet.
1809	- A BRANCH IS REBASED ONTO `origin/main` ONLY, never onto another
1810	  unlanded branch: that lands the other branch's work unverified. A
1811	  branch built on a stale local main moves with `git rebase --onto
1812	  origin/main main <branch>`, which carries only its own commits.
1813	- A PID IS CHECKED BEFORE IT IS KILLED. A recorded pid is reused once
1814	  its process exits; read `ps -o command= -p <pid>` first.
1815	- A TOOL IS RUN FOR REAL ONCE BEFORE IT BECOMES A DEFAULT. Fixtures
1816	  prove the logic; a live run proves the path (a 62 MB upload hit a
1817	  30 s client timeout that no fixture could reach).
1818	- A GATE FLOOR IS RELATIVE (N − k), NEVER AN ABSOLUTE COUNT: the total
1819	  moves when a branch deletes files, and an absolute floor then fails
1820	  correct work.
1821	- A CHANGE THE COMPILER CHECKS ABOUT ITS OWN SOURCE (a renamed type, a
1822	  new license form) lands as a BRIDGE first: main's compiler must build
1823	  the branch, because the seed and the gate's own build both use it.

1825	## Working discipline
1826	
1827	- NOTHING WE RUN TAKES MORE THAN A COUPLE OF MINUTES. Every command,
1828	  build, wait and poll is bounded to ~2 minutes; the ONE exception is a
1829	  full test run, which is ~5 minutes and runs on a Sprite. No `sleep`
1830	  chains, no 10–60 minute timeouts, no loop that polls `main` or a build
1831	  to infer progress. Break work into bounded steps: kick a long job off
1832	  as ONE bounded background command, do useful work, then check ONCE. A
1833	  `work wait` for a landing is bounded to a couple of minutes per call,
1834	  never an hour, and it reads the PR's state, never `main`.
1835	  A lane that blocks for minutes waiting is a defect in the lane, not
1836	  patience. (Owner rule, 2026-10-02: an 18-minute `sleep` loop waiting on
1837	  `main` deadlocked the merge queue — main could not move because that
1838	  lane's own PR was failing the train.)
1839	
1840	- GITHUB'S RUNNERS ARE THE ONLY GATE. `tools/gate_changed.sh` is the
1841	  gate's checks in one definition — the static keepers, `fmt --check`
1842	  on the changed `.av`, `check --baseline` on every affected package —
1843	  and checks.yml runs it on every PR, plus the compiler-dependent
1844	  keepers, the seed check and the affected packages' suites.
1845	  `tools/work land`
1846	  checks formatting alone, with the compiler the worktree already
1847	  holds, and asks no other machine; a lane that wants the whole gate
1848	  before pushing runs that script through `work run`.
1849	- A GREEN PR LANDS ITSELF, AND A STALE ONE IS REFRESHED. An armed PR
1850	  that falls behind `main` is updated by the watcher
1851	  (`tools/pr_watcher.py`, `gh pr update-branch`) so "up to date" is met
1852	  without a human; the watcher also arms a green PR, names a conflict
1853	  and cancels a closed PR's run. `work status` shows each PR's check,
1854	  its merge state and whether auto-merge is armed.
1855	- MEASURE, THEN CHANGE. `make census CMD="check <pkg>"` gives EXACT
1856	  retain/release/list-write counts and, with the per-caller tables,
1857	  who causes them; `AVRA_SAMPLE=<secs> sh tools/watch.sh 6000 ./avra
1858	  …` samples. Trust the census over the sample — and read
1859	  `sample`'s output with its tree characters (`+ ! : |`) in mind,
1860	  since parsing it as plain indentation reports the wrong fn.
1861	- A GEN-N VS GEN-N+1 DIVERGENCE IS FOUND BY TRACING, NEVER GUESSED.
1862	  `AVRA_QTRACE=1` prints one stderr line per query-kernel event —
1863	  every `Memo.ask` (family, arg, reuse/compute/cycle) and
1864	  `Memo.settle` (family, arg, fingerprint) in @std/relation's
1865	  engine/answers.av, every
1866	  `Binder.declare` (name, file) in features/namespace.av, every
1867	  failed `named_type` lookup in compiler/typing/declare.av, every
1868	  file a check PARSES (`Q parse <path>`, compiler/program.av), every
1869	  ATTEMPT a derivation makes (`Q attempt <turn> hold … reading <n>`,
1870	  compiler/derive.av) — behind
1871	  `avra_qtrace` (runtime/avra_runtime.c), inert without the flag.
1872	  Run both binaries on the SAME input with `AVRA_QTRACE=1`, confirm
1873	  each is deterministic against itself (diff two runs of the same
1874	  binary — must be empty), then diff the two traces: the FIRST
1875	  differing line names the query whose answer diverged first. Add a
1876	  probe at the divergent query's own site the same way — one
1877	  `qtrace(...)` call, removed once the cause is found.
1878	- WHICH COPY FORKED IS ANSWERED BY A CLONE LOG, NEVER BY READING THE
1879	  MECHANISM'S SOURCE. `AVRA_ALIAS_LOG=1` prints one stderr line per
1880	  ACTUAL `box_clone` (`avra_cell_unique`/`avra_slot_unique`,
1881	  runtime/avra_runtime.c's `alias_log_clone` — box_clone's only two
1882	  callers, so nothing clones outside this log) — the caller's
1883	  unslid return address (`atos -o <binary> <addr>` names it, no
1884	  `-l` needed) and the cloned box's ELEMENT COUNT. THAT COUNT IS
1885	  `a->len`, NEVER the header's `len`: every list, record and enum
1886	  payload is one `AvraArray` shape (`array_clone` treats them so),
1887	  and the header's `len` is that WRAPPER STRUCT's own fixed byte
1888	  size (40, `sizeof(AvraArray)`) — constant regardless of how many
1889	  fields or elements the box holds, so reading it answers "a box
1890	  was cloned" and never "how big". The first draft of this log
1891	  read the header and every clone in a 5.2M-line run showed length
1892	  40 or 32 — a tautology, not a finding.
